1	// Plain-language layer: how each check, chart and term is explained to a non-expert.
2	import type { Artifact, Finding } from './types'
3	
4	export type Accent = 'blue' | 'lblue' | 'orange' | 'yellow' | 'pink' | 'purple' | 'green' | 'red' | 'teal' | 'grey'
5	
6	export interface ModulePlain {
7	  name: string // plain name
8	  icon: string // Font Awesome solid icon
9	  accent: Accent
10	  does: string // one line: what it does
11	  reveals: string // what it can reveal
12	  limits: string // honest limits
13	}
14	
15	export const MODULES: Record<string, ModulePlain> = {
16	  provenance: {
17	    name: 'File history',
18	    icon: 'file-shield',
19	    accent: 'lblue',
20	    does: 'Reads the labels stored inside the file: which device made it, when, where, and which apps touched it since.',
21	    reveals: 'Phone model, recording date, GPS position, and signs the file was re-saved by an editor or messaging app.',
22	    limits: 'Labels can be stripped or faked, so they are leads until something else agrees with them.',
23	  },
24	  timeline: {
25	    name: 'Frame timing',
26	    icon: 'film',
27	    accent: 'blue',
28	    does: 'Checks every frame: how evenly they are spaced, where the picture suddenly changes, and how the video was compressed.',
29	    reveals: 'Hard cuts, dropped or duplicated frames, and joins between two recordings.',
30	    limits: 'A camera that restarts or a scene with a sudden flash can look like a cut.',
31	  },
32	  spectrum: {
33	    name: 'Sound analysis',
34	    icon: 'wave-square',
35	    accent: 'teal',
36	    does: 'Turns the sound into a picture and searches it for tones, silences and sudden changes in the background noise.',
37	    reveals: 'Hidden high-pitched tones, keypad beeps, pasted-in silence, and joins between recordings.',
38	    limits: 'Heavy compression and loud music can hide quiet clues.',
39	  },
40	  enf: {
41	    name: 'Electrical hum',
42	    icon: 'bolt',
43	    accent: 'yellow',
44	    does: 'Listens for the faint hum of the power grid, which drifts in a pattern unique to each moment in time.',
45	    reveals: 'The region (50 Hz or 60 Hz grid) and sometimes the exact date and time of recording.',
46	    limits: 'Phones filter out most hum; many recordings have none to measure.',
47	  },
48	  light: {
49	    name: 'Light flicker',
50	    icon: 'lightbulb',
51	    accent: 'yellow',
52	    does: 'Finds the invisible flicker of mains-powered lamps in the picture and compares the scene lighting with the sun.',
53	    reveals: 'Which power grid the lights run on, the camera sensor speed, and whether day or night matches the claimed time.',
54	    limits: 'Needs artificial light; daylight and LED drivers without flicker give no signal.',
55	  },
56	  pulse: {
57	    name: 'Heartbeat',
58	    icon: 'heart-pulse',
59	    accent: 'pink',
60	    does: 'Reads the tiny colour changes in skin that happen with every heartbeat.',
61	    reveals: 'Whether a face belongs to a living person, and their approximate heart rate.',
62	    limits: 'Movement, make-up, compression and poor light make this a weak signal; treat it as a hint.',
63	  },
64	  tamper: {
65	    name: 'Pixel tampering',
66	    icon: 'wand-magic-sparkles',
67	    accent: 'purple',
68	    does: 'Looks for parts of a frame that were copied, pasted or saved differently from the rest.',
69	    reveals: 'Cloned objects, patched areas and inserted graphics.',
70	    limits: 'Phone compression creates its own patterns; the maps need a human eye.',
71	  },
72	  avsync: {
73	    name: 'Sound vs picture',
74	    icon: 'arrows-left-right',
75	    accent: 'teal',
76	    does: 'Lines up sharp sounds with visible events to see whether audio and video belong together.',
77	    reveals: 'Dubbed or replaced audio, and audio slipped out of time.',
78	    limits: 'Needs clear events such as claps, doors or footsteps.',
79	  },
80	  ocr: {
81	    name: 'Text in the picture',
82	    icon: 'font',
83	    accent: 'orange',
84	    does: 'Reads signs, screens, number plates and labels visible in the frames.',
85	    reveals: 'Postcodes, phone numbers, plates, web addresses and dates that place or date the video.',
86	    limits: 'Small, blurred or angled text is often missed or misread.',
87	  },
88	  transcript: {
89	    name: 'Speech',
90	    icon: 'comment-dots',
91	    accent: 'orange',
92	    does: 'Writes down what is said, with timestamps, and identifies the language.',
93	    reveals: 'Names, places and times mentioned out loud.',
94	    limits: 'Uses an online AI service; needs it switched on, and can mishear.',
95	  },
96	  vision: {
97	    name: 'AI eyewitness',
98	    icon: 'robot',
99	    accent: 'purple',
100	    does: 'An AI model looks at key frames and describes the place, time of day and notable details.',
101	    reveals: 'Leads on location, vehicles, uniforms, weather and signs of manipulation.',
102	    limits: 'AI can be confidently wrong. Everything it says is labelled as AI and needs checking.',
103	  },
104	  geo: {
105	    name: 'Location from pixels',
106	    icon: 'earth-europe',
107	    accent: 'green',
108	    does: 'Estimates where the video was filmed using only what is visible: architecture, signs, plants, road markings.',
109	    reveals: 'A likely country, region or place, with a radius of uncertainty.',
110	    limits: 'An estimate, judged blind by AI; compare it with GPS when the file has it.',
111	  },
112	  sounds: {
113	    name: 'Sound sleuth',
114	    icon: 'ear-listen',
115	    accent: 'teal',
116	    does: 'An AI listener names the background sounds, accents and languages it can hear.',
117	    reveals: 'Sirens, birds, trains, announcements, crowds and voices that point to a place or a time of day.',
118	    limits: 'AI listening can mishear; each sound is a lead to check, not proof.',
119	  },
120	  weather: {
121	    name: 'Weather witness',
122	    icon: 'cloud-sun-rain',
123	    accent: 'blue',
124	    does: 'Checks the real recorded weather for the claimed place and time against what the footage shows.',
125	    reveals: 'Rain, wind, cloud and temperature that confirm or contradict when and where it was filmed.',
126	    limits: 'Needs a place and a time to look up; local showers can differ from the nearest weather station.',
127	  },
128	  brief: {
129	    name: 'Case summary',
130	    icon: 'scale-balanced',
131	    accent: 'red',
132	    does: 'Weighs every finding and writes the verdict and plain answers.',
133	    reveals: 'Whether independent checks agree, which is what makes a conclusion strong.',
134	    limits: 'Only as good as the checks underneath it.',
135	  },
136	}
137	
138	export function modulePlain(name: string, title?: string): ModulePlain {
139	  return (
140	    MODULES[name] ?? {
141	      name: title ? title.charAt(0) + title.slice(1).toLowerCase() : name,
142	      icon: 'microscope',
143	      accent: 'grey',
144	      does: 'An additional check.',
145	      reveals: '',
146	      limits: '',
147	    }
148	  )
149	}
150	
151	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- tabs
152	
153	export type TabKey =
154	  | 'overview'
155	  | 'timeline'
156	  | 'sound'
157	  | 'light'
158	  | 'picture'
159	  | 'people'
160	  | 'place'
161	  | 'text'
162	  | 'file'
163	  | 'findings'
164	  | 'method'
165	
166	export interface TabDef {
167	  key: TabKey
168	  label: string
169	  icon: string
170	  accent: Accent
171	  modules: string[]
172	  tags: string[] // findings from other modules carrying these tags are cross-listed here
173	  intro: string
174	}
175	
176	export const TABS: TabDef[] = [
177	  { key: 'overview', label: 'Overview', icon: 'eye', accent: 'red', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
178	  {
179	    key: 'timeline',
180	    label: 'Timeline',
181	    icon: 'film',
182	    accent: 'blue',
183	    modules: ['timeline'],
184	    tags: ['cut', 'splice'],
185	    intro: 'Every flagged moment in order, and the frame-by-frame measurements that reveal cuts and joins.',
186	  },
187	  {
188	    key: 'sound',
189	    label: 'Sound',
190	    icon: 'wave-square',
191	    accent: 'teal',
192	    modules: ['spectrum', 'enf', 'avsync', 'sounds'],
193	    tags: ['audio', 'dtmf', 'tone', 'sync'],
194	    intro: 'What the microphone picked up, including sounds people cannot hear and the hum of the power grid.',
195	  },
196	  {
197	    key: 'light',
198	    label: 'Light',
199	    icon: 'lightbulb',
200	    accent: 'yellow',
201	    modules: ['light'],
202	    tags: ['flicker', 'sun'],
203	    intro: 'Mains-powered lamps flicker too fast to see. That flicker, and the light of the sun, can date and place a video.',
204	  },
205	  {
206	    key: 'picture',
207	    label: 'Picture',
208	    icon: 'image',
209	    accent: 'purple',
210	    modules: ['tamper', 'vision'],
211	    tags: ['tamper', 'clone', 'scene'],
212	    intro: 'Signs that parts of the picture were altered, and what an AI eyewitness saw in the frames. Zoom in on any detail from the player.',
213	  },
214	  {
215	    key: 'people',
216	    label: 'People',
217	    icon: 'heart-pulse',
218	    accent: 'pink',
219	    modules: ['pulse'],
220	    tags: ['face', 'pulse', 'person'],
221	    intro: 'Signs of living people on camera: faces, and heartbeats read from tiny changes in skin colour.',
222	  },
223	  {
224	    key: 'place',
225	    label: 'Place',
226	    icon: 'location-dot',
227	    accent: 'green',
228	    modules: ['geo', 'weather'],
229	    tags: ['location', 'gps', 'osint', 'weather'],
230	    intro: 'Where it was filmed: the GPS stored in the file, and independent clues in the picture.',
231	  },
232	  {
233	    key: 'text',
234	    label: 'Text & speech',
235	    icon: 'comment-dots',
236	    accent: 'orange',
237	    modules: ['ocr', 'transcript'],
238	    tags: ['text', 'speech', 'language', 'contact'],
239	    intro: 'Words that appear on screen and words that are spoken.',
240	  },
241	  {
242	    key: 'file',
243	    label: 'File',
244	    icon: 'file-shield',
245	    accent: 'lblue',
246	    modules: ['provenance'],
247	    tags: ['metadata', 'software', 'editor', 'container', 'device'],
248	    intro: 'The file itself: fingerprints, every stored label, and the raw technical readout.',
249	  },
250	  { key: 'findings', label: 'All findings', icon: 'list-ol', accent: 'red', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
251	  { key: 'method', label: 'Method', icon: 'flask', accent: 'grey', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
252	]
253	
254	const MODULE_TAB: Record<string, TabKey> = {}
255	for (const t of TABS) for (const m of t.modules) MODULE_TAB[m] = t.key
256	
257	/** The tab an artifact lives in. Maps go to Place, captions to Text. */
258	export function artifactTab(a: Artifact): TabKey {
259	  if (a.kind === 'map') return 'place'
260	  if (a.kind === 'captions') return 'text'
261	  if (a.module === 'geo') return 'place'
262	  if (a.id === 'provenance:probe' || a.module === 'provenance') return 'file'
263	  return MODULE_TAB[a.module] ?? 'picture'
264	}
265	
266	export function findingInTab(f: Finding, tab: TabDef): boolean {
267	  if (tab.modules.includes(f.module)) return true
268	  if (!tab.modules.length) return false
269	  return (f.tags ?? []).some((t) => tab.tags.includes(t))
270	}
271	
272	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- artifact explanations
273	
274	const EXPLAIN: Record<string, string> = {
275	  'timeline:intervals':
276	    'Time between one frame and the next. A flat line is a steady camera clock; spikes mean frames were dropped, duplicated or joined.',
277	  'timeline:bitrate':
278	    'How much data each half-second of video uses. A sudden step can mean two recordings were joined or the file was re-encoded.',
279	  'timeline:difference':
280	    'How much the picture changes from one frame to the next. A tall, isolated spike is a hard cut: the camera could not have done that on its own.',
281	  'timeline:keyframes': 'Full reference frames the encoder stores at regular intervals. Irregular spacing hints at an edit.',
282	  'timeline:filmstrip': 'A thumbnail at regular intervals across the whole video.',
283	  'timeline:light_curve':
284	    'Average brightness of every frame. Lights switching, clouds or a cut show up as steps; a camera auto-exposing shows up as slow drift.',
285	  'spectrum:loudness':
286	    'How loud the sound is over time. Sudden drops to silence, or a jump in level with no visible cause, are worth a look.',
287	  'spectrum:spectrogram':
288	    'Sound drawn as a picture: time runs left to right, pitch from bottom (deep) to top (high), brightness is loudness. Steady horizontal lines are tones; sharp vertical breaks are cuts.',
289	  'spectrum:spectrogram_low':
290	    'The same picture zoomed into the deepest sounds (0–1,000 Hz), where electrical hum, engines and motors live.',
291	  'spectrum:noise_floor':
292	    'The quietest background level in each second. A room sounds the same throughout; a sudden step means the sound came from somewhere else.',
293	  'spectrum:waveform': 'Loudness over time.',
294	  'avsync:xcorr':
295	    'How well sharp sounds line up with visible changes at each delay. One clear peak near 0 ms means sound and picture belong together.',
296	  'light:flicker_spectrum':
297	    'Brightness ripples across the rows of the image. A peak at the right frequency is mains lighting, which reveals the power grid (50 Hz or 60 Hz).',
298	  'pulse:waveform': 'Tiny colour changes in skin over time. A regular rhythm is a heartbeat.',
299	  'pulse:bpm': 'Heart rate estimated across the video. A believable, fairly steady value suggests a living person.',
300	  'pulse:magnified': 'Left: the original. Right: skin-colour changes amplified so the pulse becomes visible.',
301	  'tamper:noise':
302	    'Sensor grain across the frame. Bright patches have grain unlike the rest of the picture, which can mean they were pasted in.',
303	  'tamper:ela':
304	    'Error-level analysis: the frame is re-saved and compared with itself. Areas edited after recording often glow because they recompress differently.',
305	  'provenance:tags': 'Every label stored inside the file, exactly as written by the device or app that made it.',
306	  'provenance:streams': 'The separate tracks inside the file (picture, sound, data) and how each is encoded.',
307	  'provenance:boxes':
308	    'The order of the building blocks ("boxes") inside the file. Cameras write them in a typical order; editors and apps rewrite it.',
309	  'provenance:probe': 'The complete raw technical readout of the file from ffprobe. Expand any branch to inspect it.',
310	  'provenance:map': 'The GPS position stored in the file. The circle is the accuracy the phone reported.',
311	  'ocr:text': 'Every piece of text read from the frames, when it first appeared, and in how many frames.',
312	  'transcript:segments': 'What was said, and when.',
313	  'vision:report': 'What the AI eyewitness wrote after looking at key frames. AI output: verify before relying on it.',
314	  'geo:map': 'Where the clues in the picture point. The circle shows how uncertain the estimate is.',
315	  'geo:intake': 'The working notes of the location search for one frame.',
316	  'geo:frame': 'A frame the location search examined.',
317	}
318	
319	const KIND_EXPLAIN: Record<string, string> = {
320	  series: 'Hover the chart to read exact values.',
321	  spectrogram: 'Time runs left to right, pitch bottom to top, brightness is loudness.',
322	  table: 'Raw values as measured.',
323	  bars: 'Longer bar = more.',
324	  map: 'Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.',
325	  image: 'Click to enlarge.',
326	  heatmap: 'Bright areas are where the check reacted most. Click to enlarge.',
327	  video: 'Press play.',
328	  text: '',
329	  captions: 'Click a line to jump to it.',
330	  json: 'Expand a branch to see what is inside.',
331	}
332	
333	export function explainArtifact(a: Artifact): string {
334	  if (EXPLAIN[a.id]) return EXPLAIN[a.id]
335	  const stem = `${a.module}:${a.name.replace(/[_\d.]+$/, '').replace(/_\d.*$/, '')}`
336	  if (EXPLAIN[stem]) return EXPLAIN[stem]
337	  const prefix = Object.keys(EXPLAIN).find((k) => a.id.startsWith(k))
338	  if (prefix) return EXPLAIN[prefix]
339	  return KIND_EXPLAIN[a.kind] ?? ''
340	}
341	
342	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- glossary (tooltips)
343	
344	export const GLOSSARY: Record<string, string> = {
345	  ENF: 'Electrical Network Frequency: the hum of the power grid, which drifts slightly in a way that can date a recording.',
346	  ELA: 'Error-level analysis: re-saving an image and comparing it with itself to find areas saved differently.',

// Plain-language layer: how each check, chart and term is explained to a non-expert.
import type { Artifact, Finding } from './types'

export type Accent = 'blue' | 'lblue' | 'orange' | 'yellow' | 'pink' | 'purple' | 'green' | 'red' | 'teal' | 'grey'

export interface ModulePlain {
  name: string // plain name
  icon: string // Font Awesome solid icon
  accent: Accent
  does: string // one line: what it does
  reveals: string // what it can reveal
  limits: string // honest limits
}

export const MODULES: Record<string, ModulePlain> = {
  provenance: {
    name: 'File history',
    icon: 'file-shield',
    accent: 'lblue',
    does: 'Reads the labels stored inside the file: which device made it, when, where, and which apps touched it since.',
    reveals: 'Phone model, recording date, GPS position, and signs the file was re-saved by an editor or messaging app.',
    limits: 'Labels can be stripped or faked, so they are leads until something else agrees with them.',
  },
  timeline: {
    name: 'Frame timing',
    icon: 'film',
    accent: 'blue',
    does: 'Checks every frame: how evenly they are spaced, where the picture suddenly changes, and how the video was compressed.',
    reveals: 'Hard cuts, dropped or duplicated frames, and joins between two recordings.',
    limits: 'A camera that restarts or a scene with a sudden flash can look like a cut.',
  },
  spectrum: {
    name: 'Sound analysis',
    icon: 'wave-square',
    accent: 'teal',
    does: 'Turns the sound into a picture and searches it for tones, silences and sudden changes in the background noise.',
    reveals: 'Hidden high-pitched tones, keypad beeps, pasted-in silence, and joins between recordings.',
    limits: 'Heavy compression and loud music can hide quiet clues.',
  },
  enf: {
    name: 'Electrical hum',
    icon: 'bolt',
    accent: 'yellow',
    does: 'Listens for the faint hum of the power grid, which drifts in a pattern unique to each moment in time.',
    reveals: 'The region (50 Hz or 60 Hz grid) and sometimes the exact date and time of recording.',
    limits: 'Phones filter out most hum; many recordings have none to measure.',
  },
  light: {
    name: 'Light flicker',
    icon: 'lightbulb',
    accent: 'yellow',
    does: 'Finds the invisible flicker of mains-powered lamps in the picture and compares the scene lighting with the sun.',
    reveals: 'Which power grid the lights run on, the camera sensor speed, and whether day or night matches the claimed time.',
    limits: 'Needs artificial light; daylight and LED drivers without flicker give no signal.',
  },
  pulse: {
    name: 'Heartbeat',
    icon: 'heart-pulse',
    accent: 'pink',
    does: 'Reads the tiny colour changes in skin that happen with every heartbeat.',
    reveals: 'Whether a face belongs to a living person, and their approximate heart rate.',
    limits: 'Movement, make-up, compression and poor light make this a weak signal; treat it as a hint.',
  },
  tamper: {
    name: 'Pixel tampering',
    icon: 'wand-magic-sparkles',
    accent: 'purple',
    does: 'Looks for parts of a frame that were copied, pasted or saved differently from the rest.',
    reveals: 'Cloned objects, patched areas and inserted graphics.',
    limits: 'Phone compression creates its own patterns; the maps need a human eye.',
  },
  avsync: {
    name: 'Sound vs picture',
    icon: 'arrows-left-right',
    accent: 'teal',
    does: 'Lines up sharp sounds with visible events to see whether audio and video belong together.',
    reveals: 'Dubbed or replaced audio, and audio slipped out of time.',
    limits: 'Needs clear events such as claps, doors or footsteps.',
  },
  ocr: {
    name: 'Text in the picture',
    icon: 'font',
    accent: 'orange',
    does: 'Reads signs, screens, number plates and labels visible in the frames.',
    reveals: 'Postcodes, phone numbers, plates, web addresses and dates that place or date the video.',
    limits: 'Small, blurred or angled text is often missed or misread.',
  },
  transcript: {
    name: 'Speech',
    icon: 'comment-dots',
    accent: 'orange',
    does: 'Writes down what is said, with timestamps, and identifies the language.',
    reveals: 'Names, places and times mentioned out loud.',
    limits: 'Uses an online AI service; needs it switched on, and can mishear.',
  },
  vision: {
    name: 'AI eyewitness',
    icon: 'robot',
    accent: 'purple',
    does: 'An AI model looks at key frames and describes the place, time of day and notable details.',
    reveals: 'Leads on location, vehicles, uniforms, weather and signs of manipulation.',
    limits: 'AI can be confidently wrong. Everything it says is labelled as AI and needs checking.',
  },
  geo: {
    name: 'Location from pixels',
    icon: 'earth-europe',
    accent: 'green',
    does: 'Estimates where the video was filmed using only what is visible: architecture, signs, plants, road markings.',
    reveals: 'A likely country, region or place, with a radius of uncertainty.',
    limits: 'An estimate, judged blind by AI; compare it with GPS when the file has it.',
  },
  sounds: {
    name: 'Sound sleuth',
    icon: 'ear-listen',
    accent: 'teal',
    does: 'An AI listener names the background sounds, accents and languages it can hear.',
    reveals: 'Sirens, birds, trains, announcements, crowds and voices that point to a place or a time of day.',
    limits: 'AI listening can mishear; each sound is a lead to check, not proof.',
  },
  weather: {
    name: 'Weather witness',
    icon: 'cloud-sun-rain',
    accent: 'blue',
    does: 'Checks the real recorded weather for the claimed place and time against what the footage shows.',
    reveals: 'Rain, wind, cloud and temperature that confirm or contradict when and where it was filmed.',
    limits: 'Needs a place and a time to look up; local showers can differ from the nearest weather station.',
  },
  brief: {
    name: 'Case summary',
    icon: 'scale-balanced',
    accent: 'red',
    does: 'Weighs every finding and writes the verdict and plain answers.',
    reveals: 'Whether independent checks agree, which is what makes a conclusion strong.',
    limits: 'Only as good as the checks underneath it.',
  },
}

export function modulePlain(name: string, title?: string): ModulePlain {
  return (
    MODULES[name] ?? {
      name: title ? title.charAt(0) + title.slice(1).toLowerCase() : name,
      icon: 'microscope',
      accent: 'grey',
      does: 'An additional check.',
      reveals: '',
      limits: '',
    }
  )
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- tabs

export type TabKey =
  | 'overview'
  | 'timeline'
  | 'sound'
  | 'light'
  | 'picture'
  | 'people'
  | 'place'
  | 'text'
  | 'file'
  | 'findings'
  | 'method'

export interface TabDef {
  key: TabKey
  label: string
  icon: string
  accent: Accent
  modules: string[]
  tags: string[] // findings from other modules carrying these tags are cross-listed here
  intro: string
}

export const TABS: TabDef[] = [
  { key: 'overview', label: 'Overview', icon: 'eye', accent: 'red', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
  {
    key: 'timeline',
    label: 'Timeline',
    icon: 'film',
    accent: 'blue',
    modules: ['timeline'],
    tags: ['cut', 'splice'],
    intro: 'Every flagged moment in order, and the frame-by-frame measurements that reveal cuts and joins.',
  },
  {
    key: 'sound',
    label: 'Sound',
    icon: 'wave-square',
    accent: 'teal',
    modules: ['spectrum', 'enf', 'avsync', 'sounds'],
    tags: ['audio', 'dtmf', 'tone', 'sync'],
    intro: 'What the microphone picked up, including sounds people cannot hear and the hum of the power grid.',
  },
  {
    key: 'light',
    label: 'Light',
    icon: 'lightbulb',
    accent: 'yellow',
    modules: ['light'],
    tags: ['flicker', 'sun'],
    intro: 'Mains-powered lamps flicker too fast to see. That flicker, and the light of the sun, can date and place a video.',
  },
  {
    key: 'picture',
    label: 'Picture',
    icon: 'image',
    accent: 'purple',
    modules: ['tamper', 'vision'],
    tags: ['tamper', 'clone', 'scene'],
    intro: 'Signs that parts of the picture were altered, and what an AI eyewitness saw in the frames. Zoom in on any detail from the player.',
  },
  {
    key: 'people',
    label: 'People',
    icon: 'heart-pulse',
    accent: 'pink',
    modules: ['pulse'],
    tags: ['face', 'pulse', 'person'],
    intro: 'Signs of living people on camera: faces, and heartbeats read from tiny changes in skin colour.',
  },
  {
    key: 'place',
    label: 'Place',
    icon: 'location-dot',
    accent: 'green',
    modules: ['geo', 'weather'],
    tags: ['location', 'gps', 'osint', 'weather'],
    intro: 'Where it was filmed: the GPS stored in the file, and independent clues in the picture.',
  },
  {
    key: 'text',
    label: 'Text & speech',
    icon: 'comment-dots',
    accent: 'orange',
    modules: ['ocr', 'transcript'],
    tags: ['text', 'speech', 'language', 'contact'],
    intro: 'Words that appear on screen and words that are spoken.',
  },
  {
    key: 'file',
    label: 'File',
    icon: 'file-shield',
    accent: 'lblue',
    modules: ['provenance'],
    tags: ['metadata', 'software', 'editor', 'container', 'device'],
    intro: 'The file itself: fingerprints, every stored label, and the raw technical readout.',
  },
  { key: 'findings', label: 'All findings', icon: 'list-ol', accent: 'red', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
  { key: 'method', label: 'Method', icon: 'flask', accent: 'grey', modules: [], tags: [], intro: '' },
]

const MODULE_TAB: Record<string, TabKey> = {}
for (const t of TABS) for (const m of t.modules) MODULE_TAB[m] = t.key

/** The tab an artifact lives in. Maps go to Place, captions to Text. */
export function artifactTab(a: Artifact): TabKey {
  if (a.kind === 'map') return 'place'
  if (a.kind === 'captions') return 'text'
  if (a.module === 'geo') return 'place'
  if (a.id === 'provenance:probe' || a.module === 'provenance') return 'file'
  return MODULE_TAB[a.module] ?? 'picture'
}

export function findingInTab(f: Finding, tab: TabDef): boolean {
  if (tab.modules.includes(f.module)) return true
  if (!tab.modules.length) return false
  return (f.tags ?? []).some((t) => tab.tags.includes(t))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- artifact explanations

const EXPLAIN: Record<string, string> = {
  'timeline:intervals':
    'Time between one frame and the next. A flat line is a steady camera clock; spikes mean frames were dropped, duplicated or joined.',
  'timeline:bitrate':
    'How much data each half-second of video uses. A sudden step can mean two recordings were joined or the file was re-encoded.',
  'timeline:difference':
    'How much the picture changes from one frame to the next. A tall, isolated spike is a hard cut: the camera could not have done that on its own.',
  'timeline:keyframes': 'Full reference frames the encoder stores at regular intervals. Irregular spacing hints at an edit.',
  'timeline:filmstrip': 'A thumbnail at regular intervals across the whole video.',
  'timeline:light_curve':
    'Average brightness of every frame. Lights switching, clouds or a cut show up as steps; a camera auto-exposing shows up as slow drift.',
  'spectrum:loudness':
    'How loud the sound is over time. Sudden drops to silence, or a jump in level with no visible cause, are worth a look.',
  'spectrum:spectrogram':
    'Sound drawn as a picture: time runs left to right, pitch from bottom (deep) to top (high), brightness is loudness. Steady horizontal lines are tones; sharp vertical breaks are cuts.',
  'spectrum:spectrogram_low':
    'The same picture zoomed into the deepest sounds (0–1,000 Hz), where electrical hum, engines and motors live.',
  'spectrum:noise_floor':
    'The quietest background level in each second. A room sounds the same throughout; a sudden step means the sound came from somewhere else.',
  'spectrum:waveform': 'Loudness over time.',
  'avsync:xcorr':
    'How well sharp sounds line up with visible changes at each delay. One clear peak near 0 ms means sound and picture belong together.',
  'light:flicker_spectrum':
    'Brightness ripples across the rows of the image. A peak at the right frequency is mains lighting, which reveals the power grid (50 Hz or 60 Hz).',
  'pulse:waveform': 'Tiny colour changes in skin over time. A regular rhythm is a heartbeat.',
  'pulse:bpm': 'Heart rate estimated across the video. A believable, fairly steady value suggests a living person.',
  'pulse:magnified': 'Left: the original. Right: skin-colour changes amplified so the pulse becomes visible.',
  'tamper:noise':
    'Sensor grain across the frame. Bright patches have grain unlike the rest of the picture, which can mean they were pasted in.',
  'tamper:ela':
    'Error-level analysis: the frame is re-saved and compared with itself. Areas edited after recording often glow because they recompress differently.',
  'provenance:tags': 'Every label stored inside the file, exactly as written by the device or app that made it.',
  'provenance:streams': 'The separate tracks inside the file (picture, sound, data) and how each is encoded.',
  'provenance:boxes':
    'The order of the building blocks ("boxes") inside the file. Cameras write them in a typical order; editors and apps rewrite it.',
  'provenance:probe': 'The complete raw technical readout of the file from ffprobe. Expand any branch to inspect it.',
  'provenance:map': 'The GPS position stored in the file. The circle is the accuracy the phone reported.',
  'ocr:text': 'Every piece of text read from the frames, when it first appeared, and in how many frames.',
  'transcript:segments': 'What was said, and when.',
  'vision:report': 'What the AI eyewitness wrote after looking at key frames. AI output: verify before relying on it.',
  'geo:map': 'Where the clues in the picture point. The circle shows how uncertain the estimate is.',
  'geo:intake': 'The working notes of the location search for one frame.',
  'geo:frame': 'A frame the location search examined.',
}

const KIND_EXPLAIN: Record<string, string> = {
  series: 'Hover the chart to read exact values.',
  spectrogram: 'Time runs left to right, pitch bottom to top, brightness is loudness.',
  table: 'Raw values as measured.',
  bars: 'Longer bar = more.',
  map: 'Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.',
  image: 'Click to enlarge.',
  heatmap: 'Bright areas are where the check reacted most. Click to enlarge.',
  video: 'Press play.',
  text: '',
  captions: 'Click a line to jump to it.',
  json: 'Expand a branch to see what is inside.',
}

export function explainArtifact(a: Artifact): string {
  if (EXPLAIN[a.id]) return EXPLAIN[a.id]
  const stem = `${a.module}:${a.name.replace(/[_\d.]+$/, '').replace(/_\d.*$/, '')}`
  if (EXPLAIN[stem]) return EXPLAIN[stem]
  const prefix = Object.keys(EXPLAIN).find((k) => a.id.startsWith(k))
  if (prefix) return EXPLAIN[prefix]
  return KIND_EXPLAIN[a.kind] ?? ''
}

  fps: 'Frame rate',
}

/** Unit for a data key, from its suffix. */
export function unitFor(key: string): string {
  if (key === 'bpm') return 'bpm'
  if (/_hz$|^hz$/.test(key)) return 'Hz'
  if (/_db$/.test(key)) return 'dB'
  if (/_ms$/.test(key)) return 'ms'
  if (/_s$/.test(key)) return 's'
  if (/_km$/.test(key)) return 'km'
  if (/_m$/.test(key)) return 'm'
  if (/_h$/.test(key)) return 'h'
  if (key === 'elevation' || key === 'azimuth' || key === 'sun_elevation') return '°'
  return ''
}

export const CONFIDENCE: Record<string, { word: string; level: number; tip: string }> = {
  strong: { word: 'Strong', level: 3, tip: 'Two or more independent checks agree.' },
  moderate: { word: 'Moderate', level: 2, tip: 'One reliable check supports this.' },
  weak: { word: 'Weak', level: 1, tip: 'A hint only, or based on labels that can be faked.' },
  unknown: { word: 'Not enough evidence', level: 0, tip: 'Nothing in the file answers this.' },
}

export const SEVERITY: Record<string, { word: string; icon: string; tip: string }> = {
  critical: { word: 'Critical', icon: 'burst', tip: 'Strong sign of editing, or highly sensitive information.' },
  warning: { word: 'Warning', icon: 'triangle-exclamation', tip: 'Suspicious, or contradicts something else.' },
  notice: { word: 'Notice', icon: 'circle-exclamation', tip: 'Worth knowing; not suspicious on its own.' },
  info: { word: 'Info', icon: 'circle-info', tip: 'Background fact about the file.' },
}

export type Verdict = 'edited' | 'possible' | 'clean' | 'running' | 'unknown'

export const VERDICT: Record<Verdict, { word: string; short: string; icon: string; line: string }> = {
  edited: { word: 'Edited', short: 'Edited', icon: 'scissors', line: 'Independent checks show this video was cut or altered.' },
  possible: { word: 'Possibly edited', short: 'Suspect', icon: 'triangle-exclamation', line: 'Something does not add up, but it is not proven.' },
  clean: { word: 'No signs of editing', short: 'Clean', icon: 'circle-check', line: 'Nothing measured suggests a cut or alteration.' },
  running: { word: 'Analysing', short: 'Analysing', icon: 'circle-notch', line: 'Checks are still running.' },
  unknown: { word: 'No verdict', short: 'No verdict', icon: 'circle-question', line: 'No summary was produced for this case.' },
}

export function verdictOf(v: unknown): Verdict {
  const s = String(v ?? '').toUpperCase()
  if (s === 'EDITED') return 'edited'
  if (s === 'POSSIBLY EDITED') return 'possible'
  if (s === 'NO SIGNS OF EDITING') return 'clean'
  return 'unknown'
}

  WHERE: 'Where',
  DEVICE: 'Device',
  PEOPLE: 'People',
  INTEGRITY: 'Editing',
  HIDDEN: 'Hidden',
  CORROBORATED: 'Cross-checked',
}

33	  const brief = state.artifacts['brief:brief'] ?? arts.find((a) => a.kind === 'brief') ?? null
34	  const fs = state.findings
35	  const order = state.moduleOrder
36	  const done = order.filter((n) => state.modules[n] && isTerminal(state.modules[n].status)).length
37	  const running = !!state.info && !state.done && done < order.length
38	  const counts: Record<string, number> = { critical: 0, warning: 0, notice: 0, info: 0 }
39	  for (const f of fs) counts[f.severity] = (counts[f.severity] ?? 0) + 1
40	
41	  const dev = firstData(fs, (f) => f.module === 'provenance' && !!f.data?.model)
42	  const device = dev ? [dev.make, dev.model].filter(Boolean).join(' ') : null
43	  const resavedF = fs.find((f) => f.tags?.includes('software') || f.tags?.includes('editor'))
44	  const resaved = resavedF ? resavedF.title.replace(/^Processed by\s*/i, '').replace(/\s*\(.*\)$/, '') : null
45	
46	  const clock = firstData(fs, (f) => !!f.data?.creation_time_utc)
47	  const gpsD = firstData(fs, (f) => f.tags?.includes('gps') && isFinite(f.data?.lat))
48	  const gridD = firstData(fs, (f) => typeof f.data?.grid_hz === 'number')

51	  const lang = firstData(fs, (f) => typeof f.data?.language === 'string')
52	
53	  const answers: Answer[] = Array.isArray(brief?.data?.answers) ? brief!.data.answers : []
54	  const current = order.find((n) => state.modules[n]?.status === 'running') ?? null
55	  const aiUsed = fs.some((f) => f.kind === 'inferred') || answers.some((a) => a.ai)
56	
57	  return {

59	    brief,

"""Tiger Data (TimescaleDB) storage: the grid-frequency record and the case index.

The database is required. Its URL comes from TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL (read from
the repo's .env); tables live in the schema named by EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA
(default ``earwitness``), which lets tests run in a throwaway schema.

Long-lived processes (the server) open a connection pool for their event loop
with ``open_pool``; anything else (CLI, demo, tests) gets a one-shot connection.
"""

import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from collections.abc import Iterable
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timezone
from typing import Any

import psycopg
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from psycopg import sql
from psycopg.rows import dict_row
from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
from psycopg_pool import AsyncConnectionPool

_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
_SCHEMA_SQL = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "schema.sql")
_IDENT = re.compile(r"^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$")

load_dotenv(os.path.join(_ROOT, ".env"))

_pools: dict[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, AsyncConnectionPool] = {}


class DatabaseNotConfigured(RuntimeError):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            "TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL is not set. Earwitness needs its Tiger Data "
            "database: put the service URL in .env (see .env.example)."
        )


def url() -> str:
    value = os.environ.get("TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL", "").strip()

    if not value:
        raise DatabaseNotConfigured()

    return value


def schema() -> str:
    name = os.environ.get("EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA", "earwitness").strip()

    if not _IDENT.match(name):
        raise ValueError(f"EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA {name!r} is not a plain identifier")

    return name


async def _configure(conn: psycopg.AsyncConnection) -> None:
    await conn.execute(
        sql.SQL("SET search_path TO {}, public").format(sql.Identifier(schema()))
    )
    await conn.commit()


async def open_pool() -> AsyncConnectionPool:
    """Open (once) a pool bound to the running event loop."""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

    if loop not in _pools:
        pool = AsyncConnectionPool(
            url(), min_size=1, max_size=5, configure=_configure, open=False
        )
        await pool.open(wait=True, timeout=30)
        _pools[loop] = pool

    return _pools[loop]


async def close_pool() -> None:
    pool = _pools.pop(asyncio.get_running_loop(), None)

    if pool is not None:
        await pool.close()


@asynccontextmanager
async def connection() -> AsyncIterator[psycopg.AsyncConnection]:
    pool = _pools.get(asyncio.get_running_loop())

    if pool is not None:
        async with pool.connection() as conn:
            yield conn

        return

    async with await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(url()) as conn:
        await _configure(conn)
        yield conn


def _statements(text: str) -> list[str]:
    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("--")]

    return [s.strip() for s in "\n".join(lines).split(";") if s.strip()]


async def migrate() -> bool:
    """Apply schema.sql if it changed since the last run; True when applied."""
    with open(_SCHEMA_SQL) as handle:
        text = handle.read()

    digest = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
    name = sql.Identifier(schema())

    # Continuous aggregates cannot be created inside a transaction.
    async with await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(url(), autocommit=True) as conn:
        await conn.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {}").format(name))
        await conn.execute(sql.SQL("SET search_path TO {}, public").format(name))
        await conn.execute(
            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version ("
            " digest TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())"
        )
        seen = await (
            await conn.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM schema_version WHERE digest = %s", [digest]
            )
        ).fetchone()

        if seen:
            return False

        for statement in _statements(text):
            await conn.execute(statement)

import asyncio
import os
import uuid

import pytest
from psycopg import sql

os.environ["EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA"] = f"test_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]}"

from earwitness import db  # noqa: E402 - must see the test schema name


async def _seed_grid() -> None:
    """Reuse the grid record already stored in the main schema (saves NESO trips)."""
    main = os.environ.get("EARWITNESS_GRID_SEED_SCHEMA", "earwitness")

    async with db.connection() as conn:
        present = await (
            await conn.execute(
                "SELECT to_regclass(%s) IS NOT NULL", [f"{main}.grid_coverage"]
            )
        ).fetchone()

        if not present[0]:
            return

        await conn.execute(
            sql.SQL(
                "INSERT INTO grid_frequency SELECT * FROM {}.grid_frequency"
                " ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING"
            ).format(sql.Identifier(main))
        )
        await conn.execute(
            sql.SQL("INSERT INTO grid_coverage SELECT * FROM {}.grid_coverage").format(
                sql.Identifier(main)
            )
        )

def database():
    asyncio.run(db.migrate())
    asyncio.run(_seed_grid())

    yield db.schema()

    asyncio.run(db.drop_schema())

"""End-to-end module tests on synthetic evidence with planted ground truth."""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess

import pytest

from earwitness import demo as fixtures
from earwitness.server.jobs import CaseStore

os.environ["EARWITNESS_OFFLINE"] = "1"
os.environ.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)


def run(tmp_path, video: str, modules: list[str], **options) -> list[dict]:
    async def go():
        store = CaseStore(str(tmp_path / "cases"))
        case = store.create(
            video, {"original_name": os.path.basename(video), **options}
        )
        shutil.copy(video, case.evidence_path)
        store.start(case, only=modules)
        await case.task

        return case.events

    events = asyncio.run(go())
    errors = [e for e in events if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] == "error"]
    assert not errors, errors[0].get("trace")

    return [e["finding"] for e in events if e["type"] == "finding"]


def titles(findings: list[dict]) -> str:
    return "\n".join(f"{f['module']}: {f['title']}" for f in findings)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def planted(tmp_path_factory):
    return fixtures.planted_video(str(tmp_path_factory.mktemp("v") / "planted.mp4"))


def test_planted_audio_anomalies(tmp_path, planted):
    findings = run(tmp_path, planted, ["timeline", "spectrum", "brief"])
    text = titles(findings)
    assert "Hidden tone at 18,500 Hz" in text
    assert "Keypad tones decoded: " + fixtures.PLANTED["dtmf"] in text
    silence = next(f for f in findings if "digital silence" in f["title"])
    assert abs(silence["time_s"] - fixtures.PLANTED["silence_at_s"]) < 0.05
    jump = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Room tone jumps"))
    assert abs(jump["time_s"] - fixtures.PLANTED["room_jump_at_s"]) <= 1
    cut = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Hard cut"))
    assert abs(cut["time_s"] - fixtures.PLANTED["cut_at_s"]) < 0.05
    assert "Edit corroborated by sound and picture" in text


def test_pulse_recovers_planted_rate(tmp_path, planted):
    findings = run(tmp_path, planted, ["pulse"])
    pulse = next(f for f in findings if f["module"] == "pulse" and "bpm" in f["title"])
    assert abs(pulse["data"]["bpm"] - fixtures.PLANTED["pulse_bpm"]) < 4


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("grid", "fps"), [(50.0, 30.0), (60.0, 25.0)])
def test_light_flicker_identifies_grid(tmp_path, grid, fps):
    video = fixtures.flicker_video(
        str(tmp_path / "flicker.mp4"), grid_hz=grid, fps=fps, readout_s=0.02
    )
    findings = run(tmp_path, video, ["light"])
    found = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Lights flicker"))
    assert f"{int(grid)} Hz grid" in found["title"]
    readout = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Sensor readout"))
    assert abs(readout["data"]["readout_ms"] - 20) < 2


def test_light_no_false_flicker(tmp_path, planted):
    findings = run(tmp_path, planted, ["light"])
    assert not any(f["title"].startswith("Lights flicker") for f in findings)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("offset", [0.0, 0.25])
def test_av_sync_offset(tmp_path, offset):
    video = fixtures.av_events_video(str(tmp_path / "av.mp4"), audio_offset_s=offset)
    findings = run(tmp_path, video, ["timeline", "spectrum", "avsync"])
    sync = next(f for f in findings if f["module"] == "avsync")
    assert abs(sync["data"]["lag_ms"] - offset * 1000) <= 40


def test_provenance_reads_gps_and_device(tmp_path, planted):
    tagged = str(tmp_path / "tagged.mov")
    subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", planted, "-c", "copy",
         "-metadata", "creation_time=2026-11-07T14:00:30Z",
         "-metadata", "com.apple.quicktime.creationdate=2026-11-07T14:00:30+0000",
         "-metadata", "com.apple.quicktime.location.ISO6709=+55.9442-003.1874+080.000/",
         "-metadata", "com.apple.quicktime.make=Apple", "-metadata", "com.apple.quicktime.model=iPhone 15",
         "-movflags", "use_metadata_tags", tagged],
        check=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    findings = run(tmp_path, tagged, ["provenance"])
    text = titles(findings)
    assert "GPS fix: 55.94420, -3.18740" in text
    assert "iPhone 15" in text
    assert "Sun " in text


def test_enf_dates_and_detects_splice(tmp_path):
    from earwitness import synth

    truth = asyncio.run(synth.create_scenario(str(tmp_path / "syn")))
    grid = str(tmp_path / "syn" / "grid.csv")
    clean = run(
        tmp_path,
        str(tmp_path / "syn" / "clip.mp4"),
        ["provenance", "enf"],
        grid_path=grid,
    )
    dated = next(f for f in clean if f["title"].startswith("ENF dates"))
    assert truth["start"][:19].replace("T", " ") in dated["title"]
    spliced = run(
        tmp_path,
        str(tmp_path / "syn" / "spliced.mp4"),
        ["provenance", "enf"],
        grid_path=grid,
    )
    assert any("phase jumps" in f["title"] for f in spliced)
    groups = next(f for f in spliced if "different times" in f["title"])
    assert len(groups["data"]["groups"]) >= 2


def test_ocr_reads_postcode_and_plate(tmp_path):
    from PIL import Image
    from PIL import ImageDraw
    from PIL import ImageFont

    font_path = "/System/Library/Fonts/Helvetica.ttc"

    if not os.path.isfile(font_path) or shutil.which("tesseract") is None:
        pytest.skip("needs tesseract and Helvetica")

    image = Image.new("RGB", (1280, 720), (51, 68, 85))
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    draw.text(
        (100, 120),
        "SCOTMID  12 Nicolson St  EH8 9DH",
        fill="white",
        font=ImageFont.truetype(font_path, 48),
    )
    draw.rectangle((400, 380, 820, 480), fill=(250, 210, 0))
    draw.text(
        (430, 395), "SN19 XKD", fill="black", font=ImageFont.truetype(font_path, 64)
    )
    png = str(tmp_path / "sign.png")
    image.save(png)
    video = str(tmp_path / "sign.mp4")
    subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-loop", "1", "-i", png, "-t", "3", "-r", "30",
         "-c:v", "libx264", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", video],
        check=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    text = titles(run(tmp_path, video, ["timeline", "ocr"]))
    assert "EH8 9DH" in text
    assert "SN19 XKD" in text


def test_events_are_json(tmp_path, planted):
    async def go():
        store = CaseStore(str(tmp_path / "cases"))
        case = store.create(planted, {})
        shutil.copy(planted, case.evidence_path)
        store.start(case, only=["provenance", "timeline", "tamper"])
        await case.task

        return case

    case = asyncio.run(go())

    with open(os.path.join(case.workdir, "events.jsonl")) as handle:
        events = [json.loads(line) for line in handle]

    assert events[-1]["type"] == "done"
    assert [e["seq"] for e in events] == list(range(len(events)))


def test_lighting_dates_silent_footage(tmp_path):
    """Lamp flicker following the real GB grid dates the footage to the second."""
    from datetime import datetime
    from datetime import timedelta
    from datetime import timezone

    from earwitness import grid_fetch

    truth = datetime(2024, 3, 12, 23, 10, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    series, _ = asyncio.run(
        grid_fetch.fetch(truth - timedelta(minutes=5), truth + timedelta(minutes=6))
    )

    if series is None:
        pytest.skip("grid record unavailable (offline)")

    offset = int((truth - series.start).total_seconds())
    raw = fixtures.grid_flicker_video(
        str(tmp_path / "raw.mp4"), series.values[offset : offset + 91]
    )
    video = str(tmp_path / "flicker.mp4")
    subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", raw, "-c", "copy",
         "-metadata", "creation_time=2024-03-12T23:31:30Z", video],
        check=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    findings = run(tmp_path, video, ["provenance", "light", "enf"])
    dated = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Lighting dates"))
    assert "2024-03-12 23:10:00" in dated["title"]
    assert any(
        f["title"] == "Metadata time contradicted by the lights" for f in findings
    )


def test_copy_move_clone_found(tmp_path):
    video = fixtures.cloned_video(str(tmp_path / "clone.mp4"))
    findings = run(tmp_path, video, ["timeline", "tamper"])
    clone = next(f for f in findings if f["title"].startswith("Cloned region"))
    dx, dy = clone["data"]["offset"]
    assert abs(abs(dx) - 300) <= 6 and abs(abs(dy) - 140) <= 6


def test_flashes_are_not_cuts(tmp_path):
    video = fixtures.av_events_video(str(tmp_path / "flash.mp4"))
    findings = run(tmp_path, video, ["timeline"])
    assert not any(f["title"].startswith("Hard cut") for f in findings)


def test_weather_reads_negations():
    from earwitness.modules.weather import _seen_conditions

    assert _seen_conditions(
        "Cloudy or hazy night; no visible rain, pavement appears dry."
    ) == (False, True)
    assert _seen_conditions("It is not raining; clear sky.") == (False, True)
    assert _seen_conditions("Heavy rain, wet pavement, umbrellas.") == (True, False)
    assert _seen_conditions("Overcast evening.") == (False, False)

24	    51: "light drizzle", 53: "drizzle", 55: "heavy drizzle", 56: "freezing drizzle", 57: "freezing drizzle",
25	    61: "light rain", 63: "rain", 65: "heavy rain", 66: "freezing rain", 67: "freezing rain",
26	    71: "light snow", 73: "snow", 75: "heavy snow", 77: "snow grains", 80: "rain showers",
27	    81: "rain showers", 82: "violent rain showers", 85: "snow showers", 86: "heavy snow showers",
28	    95: "thunderstorm", 96: "thunderstorm with hail", 99: "thunderstorm with hail",

"""Weather witness: what the sky was really doing there and then.

If the place (GPS, or a verified geolocation) and the time (metadata that is
not a copy stamp, or an ENF date) are known, fetch the recorded weather for
that hour from Open-Meteo's historical archive and compare it with what the
AI analyst sees in the frames. Rain in the record and a dry, sunny video (or
the reverse) means the claimed time or place is wrong.
"""

import re
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone
from typing import Any

import httpx

from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext
from earwitness.modules.base import Reporter
from earwitness.modules.base import Skip

_CODES = {
    0: "clear sky", 1: "mainly clear", 2: "partly cloudy", 3: "overcast", 45: "fog", 48: "freezing fog",
    51: "light drizzle", 53: "drizzle", 55: "heavy drizzle", 56: "freezing drizzle", 57: "freezing drizzle",
    61: "light rain", 63: "rain", 65: "heavy rain", 66: "freezing rain", 67: "freezing rain",
    71: "light snow", 73: "snow", 75: "heavy snow", 77: "snow grains", 80: "rain showers",
    81: "rain showers", 82: "violent rain showers", 85: "snow showers", 86: "heavy snow showers",
    95: "thunderstorm", 96: "thunderstorm with hail", 99: "thunderstorm with hail",
}  # fmt: skip
_WET_WORDS = ("rain", "wet", "drizzle", "puddle", "umbrella", "snow", "shower", "storm")
_DRY_WORDS = ("dry", "sunny", "clear sky", "clear, ", "bright sun")


_NEGATED = re.compile(
    r"\b(no|not|without|isn't|aren't|nor|never|free of)\b(\s+\w+){0,3}?\s+"
    r"(rain\w*|wet|drizzle|puddles?|umbrellas?|snow\w*|showers?|storms?)\b"
)


def _seen_conditions(seen: str) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    """(looks wet, looks dry) from the analyst's words, ignoring negations
    such as "no visible rain" or "not raining"."""
    text = _NEGATED.sub(" ", seen.lower())
    wet = any(w in text for w in _WET_WORDS)
    dry = (any(w in text for w in _DRY_WORDS) or "dry" in text) and not wet

    return wet, dry


async def _hourly(lat: float, lon: float, when: datetime) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    day = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).date()
    params = {
        "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon, "start_date": day.isoformat(), "end_date": day.isoformat(),
        "hourly": "temperature_2m,precipitation,cloud_cover,weather_code,wind_speed_10m,is_day",
        "timezone": "UTC",
    }  # fmt: skip
    recent = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() - day < timedelta(days=6)
    url = (
        "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"
        if recent
        else "https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive"
    )

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=15) as client:
            response = await client.get(url, params=params)
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()["hourly"]
    except httpx.HTTPError, KeyError, ValueError:
        return None

    hour = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).hour

    if hour >= len(data.get("time", [])):
        return None

    return {key: values[hour] for key, values in data.items()} | {"source": url}


class Weather:
    name = "weather"
    title = "WEATHER WITNESS"
    description = "Real recorded weather at the claimed place and time, checked against what the video shows."
    depends = ["provenance", "enf", "geo", "vision"]

    async def run(self, ctx: CaseContext, out: Reporter) -> None:
        provenance = await ctx.wait_for("provenance") or {}
        enf = await ctx.wait_for("enf") or {}
        geo = await ctx.wait_for("geo") or {}
        place, place_source = None, None

        if provenance.get("location"):
            place, place_source = provenance["location"], "the file's GPS"
        elif geo.get("verified"):
            place, place_source = (
                {"lat": geo["latitude"], "lon": geo["longitude"]},
                "the verified geolocation",
            )

        when, when_source = None, None

        if enf.get("confident") and enf.get("dated_start"):
            when, when_source = enf["dated_start"], "the power-grid dating"
        elif provenance.get("start_guess"):
            when, when_source = provenance["start_guess"], "the file's own timestamp"

        if isinstance(when, str):
            when = datetime.fromisoformat(when)

        if place is None or when is None:
            raise Skip("needs both a place and a trustworthy time")

        out.progress(0.3, "fetching the weather record")
        record = await _hourly(float(place["lat"]), float(place["lon"]), when)

        if record is None:
            raise Skip("no weather record for that place and hour")

        sky = _CODES.get(int(record.get("weather_code") or 0), "unknown")
        summary = (
            f"{record['temperature_2m']:.0f}°C, {sky}, {record['precipitation']:.1f} mm of rain that hour, "
            f"{record['cloud_cover']:.0f}% cloud, wind {record['wind_speed_10m']:.0f} km/h, "
            f"{'daylight' if record.get('is_day') else 'dark'}"
        )
        out.artifact(
            "record",
            "table",
            "Recorded weather for that place and hour",
            data={
                "columns": ["measure", "value"],
                "rows": [[k, v] for k, v in record.items()],
            },
        )
        vision = await ctx.wait_for("vision") or {}
        seen = f"{vision.get('weather', '')} {vision.get('scene', '')}".lower()
        wet_record = float(record.get("precipitation") or 0) >= 0.5 or sky.endswith(
            ("rain", "drizzle", "showers")
        )
        dry_record = (
            float(record.get("precipitation") or 0) == 0
            and int(record.get("weather_code") or 0) <= 2
        )
        wet_seen, dry_seen = _seen_conditions(seen)
        contradiction = (wet_record and dry_seen) or (dry_record and wet_seen)
        detail = (
            f"At {when:%Y-%m-%d %H:00} UTC at that spot (place from {place_source}, time from "
            f"{when_source}) the weather record says: {summary}."
        )

        if seen.strip():
            detail += f" The AI analyst sees: {vision.get('weather') or 'no weather described'}."

        out.finding(
            "warning" if contradiction else "info",
            "Weather contradicts the claimed time or place"
            if contradiction
            else f"Weather there and then: {sky}, {record['temperature_2m']:.0f}°C",
            detail
            + (
                " These do not fit together: either the time, the place, or the footage is not what it claims."
                if contradiction
                else ""
            ),
            tags=["weather", "time", "location"]
            + (["inconsistency"] if contradiction else []),
            data=record
            | {"sky": sky, "place_source": place_source, "time_source": when_source},
        )
        ctx.publish(self.name, record | {"sky": sky, "contradiction": contradiction})
        out.progress(1.0)

1	// Pull the headline facts out of the event stream, defensively (fields vary by case and backend version).
2	import type { Answer, Artifact, Finding } from './types'
3	import type { CaseState } from './state'
4	import { isTerminal } from './state'
5	import { verdictOf, type Verdict } from './plain'
6	
7	export interface Facts {
8	  verdict: Verdict
9	  brief: Artifact | null
10	  answers: Answer[]
11	  summary: string | null
12	  running: boolean
13	  checksDone: number
14	  checksTotal: number
15	  counts: Record<string, number>
16	  device: string | null
17	  software: string | null
18	  resaved: string | null
19	  recorded: string | null
20	  gps: { lat: number; lon: number; accuracy_m?: number; place?: string; alt_m?: number } | null
21	  grid: number | null
22	  pulse: number | null
23	  language: string | null
24	  aiUsed: boolean
25	  hasAudio: boolean
26	  currentModule: string | null
27	}
28	
29	const firstData = (findings: Finding[], pred: (f: Finding) => boolean) => findings.find(pred)?.data ?? null
30	
31	export function deriveFacts(state: CaseState, openai: boolean | null): Facts {
32	  const arts = state.artifactOrder.map((id) => state.artifacts[id])
33	  const brief = state.artifacts['brief:brief'] ?? arts.find((a) => a.kind === 'brief') ?? null
34	  const fs = state.findings
35	  const order = state.moduleOrder
36	  const done = order.filter((n) => state.modules[n] && isTerminal(state.modules[n].status)).length
37	  const running = !!state.info && !state.done && done < order.length
38	  const counts: Record<string, number> = { critical: 0, warning: 0, notice: 0, info: 0 }
39	  for (const f of fs) counts[f.severity] = (counts[f.severity] ?? 0) + 1
40	
41	  const dev = firstData(fs, (f) => f.module === 'provenance' && !!f.data?.model)
42	  const device = dev ? [dev.make, dev.model].filter(Boolean).join(' ') : null
43	  const resavedF = fs.find((f) => f.tags?.includes('software') || f.tags?.includes('editor'))
44	  const resaved = resavedF ? resavedF.title.replace(/^Processed by\s*/i, '').replace(/\s*\(.*\)$/, '') : null
45	
46	  const clock = firstData(fs, (f) => !!f.data?.creation_time_utc)
47	  const gpsD = firstData(fs, (f) => f.tags?.includes('gps') && isFinite(f.data?.lat))
48	  const gridD = firstData(fs, (f) => typeof f.data?.grid_hz === 'number')
49	  const nominal = fs.find((f) => /\b(50|60) Hz grid\b/.test(f.title))
50	  const pulseD = firstData(fs, (f) => f.module === 'pulse' && typeof f.data?.bpm === 'number')
51	  const lang = firstData(fs, (f) => typeof f.data?.language === 'string')
52	
53	  const answers: Answer[] = Array.isArray(brief?.data?.answers) ? brief!.data.answers : []
54	  const current = order.find((n) => state.modules[n]?.status === 'running') ?? null
55	  const aiUsed = fs.some((f) => f.kind === 'inferred') || answers.some((a) => a.ai)
56	
57	  return {
58	    verdict: state.error ? 'unknown' : running && !brief ? 'running' : brief ? verdictOf(brief.data?.verdict) : state.done ? 'unknown' : 'running',
59	    brief,
60	    answers,
61	    summary: brief?.data?.summary_plain ?? brief?.data?.headline ?? null,
62	    running,
63	    checksDone: done,
64	    checksTotal: order.length,
65	    counts,
66	    device,
67	    software: dev?.software ?? null,
68	    resaved,
69	    recorded: clock?.creation_time_utc ?? null,
70	    gps: gpsD ? { lat: gpsD.lat, lon: gpsD.lon, accuracy_m: gpsD.accuracy_m, place: gpsD.place, alt_m: gpsD.alt_m } : null,
71	    grid: gridD?.grid_hz ?? (nominal ? Number(nominal.title.match(/\b(50|60) Hz grid/)![1]) : null),
72	    pulse: pulseD ? Math.round(pulseD.bpm) : null,
73	    language: lang?.language ?? null,
74	    aiUsed: aiUsed || !!openai,
75	    hasAudio: !!state.info?.has_audio,
76	    currentModule: current,
77	  }
78	}

80	/** Severity rank then time, for the findings "leaderboard". */
81	export function rankFindings(fs: Finding[]): Finding[] {
82	  const sev: Record<string, number> = { critical: 0, warning: 1, notice: 2, info: 3 }
83	  return [...fs].sort(
84	    (a, b) => (sev[a.severity] ?? 9) - (sev[b.severity] ?? 9) || (a.time_s ?? 1e9) - (b.time_s ?? 1e9) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id),
85	  )
86	}

1	"""Tiger Data (TimescaleDB) storage: the grid-frequency record and the case index.
2	
3	The database is required. Its URL comes from TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL (read from
4	the repo's .env); tables live in the schema named by EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA
5	(default ``earwitness``), which lets tests run in a throwaway schema.
6	
7	Long-lived processes (the server) open a connection pool for their event loop
8	with ``open_pool``; anything else (CLI, demo, tests) gets a one-shot connection.
9	"""
10	
11	import asyncio
12	import hashlib
13	import json
14	import os
15	import re
16	from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
17	from collections.abc import Iterable
18	from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
19	from datetime import datetime
20	from datetime import timezone
21	from typing import Any
22	
23	import psycopg
24	from dotenv import load_dotenv
25	from psycopg import sql
26	from psycopg.rows import dict_row
27	from psycopg.types.json import Jsonb
28	from psycopg_pool import AsyncConnectionPool
29	
30	_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
31	_SCHEMA_SQL = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "schema.sql")
32	_IDENT = re.compile(r"^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]{0,62}$")
33	
34	load_dotenv(os.path.join(_ROOT, ".env"))
35	
36	_pools: dict[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop, AsyncConnectionPool] = {}
37	
38	
39	class DatabaseNotConfigured(RuntimeError):
40	    def __init__(self) -> None:
41	        super().__init__(
42	            "TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL is not set. Earwitness needs its Tiger Data "
43	            "database: put the service URL in .env (see .env.example)."
44	        )
45	
46	
47	def url() -> str:
48	    value = os.environ.get("TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL", "").strip()
49	
50	    if not value:
51	        raise DatabaseNotConfigured()
52	
53	    return value
54	
55	
56	def schema() -> str:
57	    name = os.environ.get("EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA", "earwitness").strip()
58	
59	    if not _IDENT.match(name):
60	        raise ValueError(f"EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA {name!r} is not a plain identifier")
61	
62	    return name
63	
64	
65	async def _configure(conn: psycopg.AsyncConnection) -> None:
66	    await conn.execute(
67	        sql.SQL("SET search_path TO {}, public").format(sql.Identifier(schema()))
68	    )
69	    await conn.commit()
70	
71	
72	async def open_pool() -> AsyncConnectionPool:
73	    """Open (once) a pool bound to the running event loop."""
74	    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
75	
76	    if loop not in _pools:
77	        pool = AsyncConnectionPool(
78	            url(), min_size=1, max_size=5, configure=_configure, open=False
79	        )
80	        await pool.open(wait=True, timeout=30)
81	        _pools[loop] = pool
82	
83	    return _pools[loop]
84	
85	
86	async def close_pool() -> None:
87	    pool = _pools.pop(asyncio.get_running_loop(), None)
88	
89	    if pool is not None:
90	        await pool.close()
91	
92	
93	@asynccontextmanager
94	async def connection() -> AsyncIterator[psycopg.AsyncConnection]:
95	    pool = _pools.get(asyncio.get_running_loop())
96	
97	    if pool is not None:
98	        async with pool.connection() as conn:
99	            yield conn
100	
101	        return
102	
103	    async with await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(url()) as conn:
104	        await _configure(conn)
105	        yield conn
106	
107	
108	def _statements(text: str) -> list[str]:
109	    lines = [line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("--")]
110	
111	    return [s.strip() for s in "\n".join(lines).split(";") if s.strip()]
112	
113	
114	async def migrate() -> bool:
115	    """Apply schema.sql if it changed since the last run; True when applied."""
116	    with open(_SCHEMA_SQL) as handle:
117	        text = handle.read()
118	
119	    digest = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
120	    name = sql.Identifier(schema())
121	
122	    # Continuous aggregates cannot be created inside a transaction.
123	    async with await psycopg.AsyncConnection.connect(url(), autocommit=True) as conn:
124	        await conn.execute(sql.SQL("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {}").format(name))
125	        await conn.execute(sql.SQL("SET search_path TO {}, public").format(name))
126	        await conn.execute(
127	            "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version ("
128	            " digest TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())"
129	        )
130	        seen = await (
131	            await conn.execute(
132	                "SELECT 1 FROM schema_version WHERE digest = %s", [digest]
133	            )
134	        ).fetchone()
135	
136	        if seen:
137	            return False
138	
139	        for statement in _statements(text):
140	            await conn.execute(statement)

1	"""Weather witness: what the sky was really doing there and then.
2	
3	If the place (GPS, or a verified geolocation) and the time (metadata that is
4	not a copy stamp, or an ENF date) are known, fetch the recorded weather for
5	that hour from Open-Meteo's historical archive and compare it with what the
6	AI analyst sees in the frames. Rain in the record and a dry, sunny video (or
7	the reverse) means the claimed time or place is wrong.
8	"""
9	
10	import re
11	from datetime import datetime
12	from datetime import timedelta
13	from datetime import timezone
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	import httpx
17	
18	from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext

22	_CODES = {
23	    0: "clear sky", 1: "mainly clear", 2: "partly cloudy", 3: "overcast", 45: "fog", 48: "freezing fog",
24	    51: "light drizzle", 53: "drizzle", 55: "heavy drizzle", 56: "freezing drizzle", 57: "freezing drizzle",
25	    61: "light rain", 63: "rain", 65: "heavy rain", 66: "freezing rain", 67: "freezing rain",
26	    71: "light snow", 73: "snow", 75: "heavy snow", 77: "snow grains", 80: "rain showers",
27	    81: "rain showers", 82: "violent rain showers", 85: "snow showers", 86: "heavy snow showers",
28	    95: "thunderstorm", 96: "thunderstorm with hail", 99: "thunderstorm with hail",
29	}  # fmt: skip
30	_WET_WORDS = ("rain", "wet", "drizzle", "puddle", "umbrella", "snow", "shower", "storm")
31	_DRY_WORDS = ("dry", "sunny", "clear sky", "clear, ", "bright sun")
32	
33	
34	_NEGATED = re.compile(
35	    r"\b(no|not|without|isn't|aren't|nor|never|free of)\b(\s+\w+){0,3}?\s+"
36	    r"(rain\w*|wet|drizzle|puddles?|umbrellas?|snow\w*|showers?|storms?)\b"
37	)
38	
39	
40	def _seen_conditions(seen: str) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
41	    """(looks wet, looks dry) from the analyst's words, ignoring negations
42	    such as "no visible rain" or "not raining"."""
43	    text = _NEGATED.sub(" ", seen.lower())
44	    wet = any(w in text for w in _WET_WORDS)
45	    dry = (any(w in text for w in _DRY_WORDS) or "dry" in text) and not wet
46	
47	    return wet, dry

50	async def _hourly(lat: float, lon: float, when: datetime) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
51	    day = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).date()
52	    params = {
53	        "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon, "start_date": day.isoformat(), "end_date": day.isoformat(),
54	        "hourly": "temperature_2m,precipitation,cloud_cover,weather_code,wind_speed_10m,is_day",
55	        "timezone": "UTC",
56	    }  # fmt: skip
57	    recent = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date() - day < timedelta(days=6)
58	    url = (
59	        "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"
60	        if recent
61	        else "https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive"
62	    )
63	
64	    try:
65	        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=15) as client:
66	            response = await client.get(url, params=params)
67	            response.raise_for_status()
68	            data = response.json()["hourly"]
69	    except httpx.HTTPError, KeyError, ValueError:
70	        return None
71	
72	    hour = when.astimezone(timezone.utc).hour
73	
74	    if hour >= len(data.get("time", [])):
75	        return None
76	
77	    return {key: values[hour] for key, values in data.items()} | {"source": url}

80	class Weather:
81	    name = "weather"
82	    title = "WEATHER WITNESS"
83	    description = "Real recorded weather at the claimed place and time, checked against what the video shows."
84	    depends = ["provenance", "enf", "geo", "vision"]
85	
86	    async def run(self, ctx: CaseContext, out: Reporter) -> None:
87	        provenance = await ctx.wait_for("provenance") or {}
88	        enf = await ctx.wait_for("enf") or {}
89	        geo = await ctx.wait_for("geo") or {}
90	        place, place_source = None, None
91	
92	        if provenance.get("location"):
93	            place, place_source = provenance["location"], "the file's GPS"
94	        elif geo.get("verified"):
95	            place, place_source = (
96	                {"lat": geo["latitude"], "lon": geo["longitude"]},
97	                "the verified geolocation",
98	            )
99	
100	        when, when_source = None, None
101	
102	        if enf.get("confident") and enf.get("dated_start"):
103	            when, when_source = enf["dated_start"], "the power-grid dating"
104	        elif provenance.get("start_guess"):
105	            when, when_source = provenance["start_guess"], "the file's own timestamp"
106	
107	        if isinstance(when, str):
108	            when = datetime.fromisoformat(when)
109	
110	        if place is None or when is None:
111	            raise Skip("needs both a place and a trustworthy time")
112	
113	        out.progress(0.3, "fetching the weather record")
114	        record = await _hourly(float(place["lat"]), float(place["lon"]), when)
115	
116	        if record is None:
117	            raise Skip("no weather record for that place and hour")
118	
119	        sky = _CODES.get(int(record.get("weather_code") or 0), "unknown")
120	        summary = (
121	            f"{record['temperature_2m']:.0f}°C, {sky}, {record['precipitation']:.1f} mm of rain that hour, "
122	            f"{record['cloud_cover']:.0f}% cloud, wind {record['wind_speed_10m']:.0f} km/h, "
123	            f"{'daylight' if record.get('is_day') else 'dark'}"
124	        )
125	        out.artifact(
126	            "record",
127	            "table",
128	            "Recorded weather for that place and hour",
129	            data={
130	                "columns": ["measure", "value"],
131	                "rows": [[k, v] for k, v in record.items()],
132	            },
133	        )
134	        vision = await ctx.wait_for("vision") or {}
135	        seen = f"{vision.get('weather', '')} {vision.get('scene', '')}".lower()
136	        wet_record = float(record.get("precipitation") or 0) >= 0.5 or sky.endswith(
137	            ("rain", "drizzle", "showers")
138	        )
139	        dry_record = (
140	            float(record.get("precipitation") or 0) == 0
141	            and int(record.get("weather_code") or 0) <= 2
142	        )
143	        wet_seen, dry_seen = _seen_conditions(seen)
144	        contradiction = (wet_record and dry_seen) or (dry_record and wet_seen)
145	        detail = (
146	            f"At {when:%Y-%m-%d %H:00} UTC at that spot (place from {place_source}, time from "
147	            f"{when_source}) the weather record says: {summary}."
148	        )
149	
150	        if seen.strip():
151	            detail += f" The AI analyst sees: {vision.get('weather') or 'no weather described'}."
152	
153	        out.finding(
154	            "warning" if contradiction else "info",
155	            "Weather contradicts the claimed time or place"
156	            if contradiction
157	            else f"Weather there and then: {sky}, {record['temperature_2m']:.0f}°C",
158	            detail
159	            + (
160	                " These do not fit together: either the time, the place, or the footage is not what it claims."
161	                if contradiction
162	                else ""
163	            ),
164	            tags=["weather", "time", "location"]
165	            + (["inconsistency"] if contradiction else []),
166	            data=record
167	            | {"sky": sky, "place_source": place_source, "time_source": when_source},
168	        )
169	        ctx.publish(self.name, record | {"sky": sky, "contradiction": contradiction})
170	        out.progress(1.0)

---SCHEMA
-- Earwitness schema. Applied by earwitness.db.migrate() inside the schema named
-- by EARWITNESS_DB_SCHEMA (search_path is set first), so nothing here is
-- schema-qualified. Every statement must be idempotent.

-- GB grid frequency, one row per sample, from every source we have fetched.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS grid_frequency (
    time   TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL,
    source TEXT             NOT NULL,
    hz     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (source, time)
) WITH (
    tsdb.hypertable,
    tsdb.segmentby = 'source',
    tsdb.orderby = 'time DESC'
);

-- Windows already fetched from a source: tells "never fetched" apart from
-- "fetched and complete", so a covered window needs no HTTP at all.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS grid_coverage (
    source     TEXT        NOT NULL,
    start_ts   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    end_ts     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    fetched_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS grid_coverage_span ON grid_coverage (source, start_ts, end_ts);

-- Minute summary of the grid record, kept fresh by TimescaleDB.
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS grid_frequency_1m
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', time) AS bucket,
       source,
       avg(hz) AS avg_hz,
       min(hz) AS min_hz,
       max(hz) AS max_hz,
       count(*) AS samples
FROM grid_frequency
GROUP BY bucket, source
WITH NO DATA;

-- Real-time: windows stored since the last refresh are included straight away.
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW grid_frequency_1m SET (timescaledb.materialized_only = false);

SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
    'grid_frequency_1m',
    start_offset => NULL,
    end_offset => INTERVAL '1 minute',
    schedule_interval => INTERVAL '10 minutes',
    if_not_exists => true
);

-- Index of every analysed clip. events.jsonl stays the replay source of truth.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cases (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    filename      TEXT        NOT NULL,
    created       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    status        TEXT        NOT NULL,
    sha256        TEXT,
    duration_s    DOUBLE PRECISION,
    verdict       TEXT,
    summary_plain TEXT,
    dated_start   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    options       JSONB       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS cases_dated_start ON cases (dated_start);

-- Every finding of every case, on the time it was reported.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS findings (
    time       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    case_id    TEXT        NOT NULL,
    finding_id TEXT        NOT NULL,
    module     TEXT        NOT NULL,
    severity   TEXT        NOT NULL,
    title      TEXT        NOT NULL,
    detail     TEXT,
    tags       TEXT[]      NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    data       JSONB       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    PRIMARY KEY (case_id, finding_id, time)
) WITH (
    tsdb.hypertable,
    tsdb.segmentby = 'case_id',
    tsdb.orderby = 'time DESC'
);
