                )  # fmt: skip
                fraction = float((full[covered] > 0.5 * full[covered].max()).mean()) if covered.any() else 0.0

                if 0.05 < fraction < 0.6 and covered.any():
                    ys, xs = np.where(full > 0.5 * full[covered].max())
                    box = photo.box_fraction(xs.min() * 16, ys.min() * 16, (xs.max() - xs.min() + 1) * 16, (ys.max() - ys.min() + 1) * 16, image.shape[1], image.shape[0])
                    region_words = f" The ghost is concentrated in one part of the picture (about {fraction * 100:.0f}% of the sampled area), which is how a region pasted in from a quality-{quality} JPEG looks."
                    published["ghost_region"] = box
                else:
                    box = None
            else:
                box = None

            out.finding(
                "warning" if best["depth"] >= 0.15 or box else "notice",
                f"Compressed twice: traces of an earlier save at quality ≈ {quality}",
                f"Recompressing the picture at every quality shows a dip of {best['depth'] * 100:.0f}% at quality {quality}, apart from the file's own quality"
                f"{f' ({current})' if current else ''}. A picture saved once has one dip; a second dip is the ghost of an earlier JPEG save.{region_words}",
                tags=["jpeg", "resaved", "double-compression"] + (["splice", "tamper"] if box else []),
                data={"earlier_quality": quality, "depth": best["depth"], "current_quality": current, "all_dips": dips, "box": box} if box else
                     {"earlier_quality": quality, "depth": best["depth"], "current_quality": current, "all_dips": dips},
            )  # fmt: skip
        elif jpeg is not None:
            out.finding(
                "info",
                "No ghost of an earlier JPEG save",
                "Recompressing at every quality shows a single dip at the file's own quality. Nothing points to a second JPEG generation"
                " (a re-save at a much higher quality than the first would hide one).",
                tags=["jpeg"],
                data={"dips": dips},
            )

        # ---- block grid -------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.7, "measuring the 8×8 block grid")
        col_profile, row_profile = await asyncio.to_thread(grid_profile, gray)
        phase_x, strength_x = grid_strength(col_profile)
        phase_y, strength_y = grid_strength(row_profile)
        strength = min(strength_x, strength_y)
        out.artifact(
            "grid_profile", "bars", "Edge energy by pixel position within the 8×8 grid",
            data={"labels": [f"col {k}" for k in range(8)] + [f"row {k}" for k in range(8)],
                  "values": np.round(np.concatenate([col_profile, row_profile]), 4).tolist()},
        )  # fmt: skip
        published["grid"] = {"phase": [phase_x, phase_y], "strength": strength}

        if jpeg is None and strength > 3.0 and phase_x == 0 and phase_y == 0:
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                f"This {info.format} was once a JPEG",
                f"An 8×8 block grid shows through the pixels ({strength:.1f} σ above the other positions). {info.format} is lossless and leaves no grid; "
                "the picture was a JPEG before it was converted. Screenshots of JPEGs and re-saved downloads look like this.",
                tags=["jpeg", "resaved", "converted"],
                data={"strength": strength, "col_profile": col_profile.tolist(), "row_profile": row_profile.tolist()},
            )
        elif jpeg is None and strength > 3.0:
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                f"JPEG grid offset by ({phase_x}, {phase_y}) pixels in this {info.format}",
                "The picture carries an 8×8 compression grid that does not start at the corner: it was a JPEG, then cropped by a non-multiple of 8 pixels before being saved losslessly.",
                tags=["jpeg", "resaved", "cropped"],
                data={"phase": [phase_x, phase_y], "strength": strength},
            )

        # Per-tile grid phase: a pasted JPEG region keeps its own grid alignment.
        if strength > 2.0 or jpeg is not None:
            grid = await asyncio.to_thread(grid_map, gray)
            strengths, phases = grid["strengths"], grid["phases"]
            confident = strengths > 4.0

            if confident.sum() >= 8:
                dominant = np.array([phase_x, phase_y]) if jpeg is not None else np.array(np.unravel_index(0, (1, 1)))
                vals, counts = np.unique(phases[confident].reshape(-1, 2), axis=0, return_counts=True)
                dominant = vals[np.argmax(counts)]
                shifted = confident & np.any(phases != dominant, axis=2)
                fraction_shifted = float(shifted.sum() / confident.sum())
                heat = np.where(shifted, np.clip(strengths / 8, 0, 1), 0).astype(np.float32)
                path = out.path("grid_map.jpg")
                photo.save_bgr(path, photo.heat_overlay(photo.fit(image, 1600), heat, cv2.COLORMAP_COOL, 0.7))
                out.artifact(
                    "grid_map", "heatmap", "Block-grid alignment map",
                    file=path, data={"caption": f"Coloured: tiles whose 8×8 grid is shifted against the dominant grid ({dominant[0]}, {dominant[1]}); dark: aligned or no grid visible", "overlay": True},
                )  # fmt: skip
                count, labels, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(shifted.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8)
                regions = [s for s in stats[1:] if s[4] >= 4]

                if regions and 0.0 < fraction_shifted < 0.5:
                    s = max(regions, key=lambda r: r[4])
                    tile = grid["tile"]
                    box = photo.box_fraction(s[0] * tile, s[1] * tile, s[2] * tile, s[3] * tile, image.shape[1], image.shape[0])
                    out.finding(
                        "warning",
                        "Region with a shifted JPEG grid",
                        f"{int(s[4])} tiles ({fraction_shifted * 100:.0f}% of the tiles where a grid is measurable) carry an 8×8 grid that does not line up with the rest of the picture. "
                        "Every block of one JPEG shares one grid; a patch with its own alignment was pasted in from another JPEG, or moved after compression.",
                        tags=["jpeg", "splice", "tamper"],
                        data={"box": box, "tiles": int(s[4]), "fraction_shifted": fraction_shifted, "dominant_phase": dominant.tolist()},
                    )
                    published["grid_region"] = box

        ctx.publish(self.name, published)
        out.progress(1.0)

"""The anatomy of the compression: what the encoder left behind.

A JPEG's quantisation tables say how hard it was compressed and which software
did it; its segment order, Huffman tables and chroma subsampling say whether a
camera or an editor wrote it. Recompressing the picture at every quality and
watching the error ("JPEG ghosts") reveals an earlier save at a different
quality, overall or in one pasted region. The 8×8 block grid that JPEG leaves
in the pixels can be found even in a PNG, and a region whose grid is shifted
was pasted in from another JPEG.
"""

import asyncio
from typing import Any

import cv2
import numpy as np

from earwitness import photo
from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext
from earwitness.modules.base import Reporter
from earwitness.modules.base import Skip
from earwitness.modules.base import downsample_series

_GHOST_QUALITIES = list(range(30, 101, 2))
_GHOST_CROP = 1024
_GRID_TILE = 96


def _aligned_crops(gray: np.ndarray, size: int, count: int = 4) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Top-left corners (multiples of 8) of up to ``count`` crops spread over the image."""
    h, w = gray.shape[:2]
    size = min(size, h - h % 8, w - w % 8)

    if size < 64:
        return [(0, 0)]

    if h <= size and w <= size:
        return [(0, 0)]

    ys = np.linspace(0, h - size, 2).astype(int) // 8 * 8
    xs = np.linspace(0, w - size, 2).astype(int) // 8 * 8
    corners = sorted({(int(y), int(x)) for y in ys for x in xs})

    return corners[:count]


def ghost_curve(rgb: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Mean squared recompression error at each quality, averaged over aligned crops."""
    corners = _aligned_crops(rgb, _GHOST_CROP)
    size = min(_GHOST_CROP, rgb.shape[0] - rgb.shape[0] % 8, rgb.shape[1] - rgb.shape[1] % 8)
    crops = [rgb[y : y + size, x : x + size] for y, x in corners]
    curve = np.zeros(len(_GHOST_QUALITIES))
    block_maps: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
    block = 16

    for index, quality in enumerate(_GHOST_QUALITIES):
        errors = []
        maps = []

        for crop in crops:
            again = photo.decode_jpeg_bytes(photo.encode_jpeg_bytes(crop, quality))

            if again is None or again.shape != crop.shape:
                continue

            diff = (crop.astype(np.float32) - again.astype(np.float32)) ** 2
            diff = diff.mean(axis=2)
            errors.append(float(diff.mean()))
            hb, wb = diff.shape[0] // block, diff.shape[1] // block
            maps.append(diff[: hb * block, : wb * block].reshape(hb, block, wb, block).mean(axis=(1, 3)))

        curve[index] = float(np.mean(errors)) if errors else np.nan
        block_maps[quality] = maps

    return {"qualities": np.array(_GHOST_QUALITIES), "curve": curve, "block_maps": block_maps, "corners": corners, "size": size}


def ghost_minima(qualities: np.ndarray, curve: np.ndarray) -> list[dict[str, float]]:
    """Local dips in the ghost curve, with their depth relative to the trend."""
    out = []
    valid = np.isfinite(curve)

    if valid.sum() < 5:
        return out

    log = np.log(curve + 1e-9)

    for i in range(2, len(curve) - 2):
        if not valid[i - 2 : i + 3].all():
            continue

        window = log[i - 2 : i + 3]
        neighbours = (log[i - 2] + log[i + 2]) / 2

        if log[i] < log[i - 1] and log[i] <= log[i + 1] and log[i] < neighbours:
            depth = float(np.exp(neighbours - log[i]) - 1)  # relative dip: 0.1 = 10% below the trend

            if depth >= 0.08 and window.argmin() == 2:
                out.append({"quality": float(qualities[i]), "depth": depth})

    return sorted(out, key=lambda d: -d["depth"])


def grid_profile(gray: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Mean |first difference| by column phase (mod 8) and by row phase."""
    g = gray.astype(np.float32)
    dx = np.abs(np.diff(g, axis=1))  # dx[:, x-1] = |g[x] - g[x-1]|, boundary before column x
    dy = np.abs(np.diff(g, axis=0))
    cols = np.arange(1, g.shape[1]) % 8
    rows = np.arange(1, g.shape[0]) % 8
    col_profile = np.array([dx[:, cols == k].mean() if (cols == k).any() else 0 for k in range(8)])
    row_profile = np.array([dy[rows == k].mean() if (rows == k).any() else 0 for k in range(8)])

    return col_profile, row_profile


def grid_strength(profile: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, float]:
    """(phase of the strongest boundary, how far it stands above the other phases, in robust sigmas)."""
    phase = int(np.argmax(profile))
    others = np.delete(profile, phase)
    spread = np.std(others) + 1e-6

    return phase, float((profile[phase] - others.mean()) / spread)


def grid_map(gray: np.ndarray, tile: int = _GRID_TILE) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per-tile JPEG grid phase and strength."""
    h, w = gray.shape
    hb, wb = h // tile, w // tile
    phases = np.zeros((hb, wb, 2), dtype=int)
    strengths = np.zeros((hb, wb))

    for by in range(hb):
        for bx in range(wb):
            patch = gray[by * tile : (by + 1) * tile, bx * tile : (bx + 1) * tile]

            if patch.std() < 2:  # flat sky or wall: no grid to see
                continue

            cp, rp = grid_profile(patch)
            px, sx = grid_strength(cp)
            py, sy = grid_strength(rp)
            phases[by, bx] = (px, py)
            strengths[by, bx] = min(sx, sy)

    return {"phases": phases, "strengths": strengths, "tile": tile}


class Compression:
    name = "jpeg"
    title = "COMPRESSION ANATOMY"
    description = "Quantisation tables and quality, encoder fingerprints, JPEG ghosts (earlier saves), and the 8×8 block grid, including shifted grids in pasted regions."

    async def run(self, ctx: CaseContext, out: Reporter) -> None:
        image = ctx.image()
        info = ctx.image_info()

        if image is None or info is None:
            raise Skip("not a decodable image")

        with open(ctx.path, "rb") as handle:
            data = handle.read()

        jpeg = photo.jpeg_anatomy(data) if data[:2] == b"\xff\xd8" else None
        published: dict[str, Any] = {"is_jpeg": jpeg is not None, "quality": None}
        gray = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
        megapixels = image.shape[0] * image.shape[1] / 1e6
        bits_per_pixel = len(data) * 8 / (image.shape[0] * image.shape[1])

        # ---- JPEG tables and encoder fingerprints -----------------------------------------
        if jpeg is not None:
            out.progress(0.1, "reading quantisation tables")
            estimate = photo.estimate_quality(jpeg.quant)

            for table_id, table in sorted(jpeg.quant.items()):
                out.artifact(
                    f"quant_{table_id}", "table",
                    f"Quantisation table {table_id} ({'luminance' if table_id == 0 else 'chrominance'})",
                    data={"columns": [f"c{i}" for i in range(8)], "rows": table.reshape(8, 8).astype(int).tolist()},
                )  # fmt: skip

            out.artifact(
                "segments", "table", "JPEG segments in file order",
                data={"columns": ["offset", "segment", "bytes", "note"],
                      "rows": [[s["offset"], s.get("app") or s["name"], s["length"], s.get("text", "") or (f"{s['scan_bytes']:,} bytes of entropy-coded data" if "scan_bytes" in s else "")] for s in jpeg.segments]},
            )  # fmt: skip

            if estimate:
                published["quality"] = estimate.quality
                published["standard_tables"] = estimate.standard_tables
                kind = "libjpeg-standard tables" if estimate.standard_tables else "custom tables"
                out.finding(
                    "info",
                    f"Saved at JPEG quality ≈ {estimate.quality} ({kind})",
                    f"The quantisation tables match libjpeg's quality {estimate.quality} scaling" + (f" to within {estimate.distance:.2f} steps" if estimate.standard_tables else f" only loosely ({estimate.distance:.1f} steps off): the encoder used its own tables") +
                    f". {jpeg.sampling} chroma subsampling, {'progressive' if jpeg.progressive else 'baseline'}, {jpeg.huffman_tables} Huffman segment{'s' if jpeg.huffman_tables != 1 else ''}"
                    f"{' (optimised)' if jpeg.optimised_huffman else ' (standard)' if jpeg.optimised_huffman is False else ''}, "
                    f"{bits_per_pixel:.2f} bits per pixel over {megapixels:.1f} megapixels"
                    + (f", restart interval {jpeg.restart_interval}" if jpeg.restart_interval else "") + ".",
                    tags=["jpeg", "quality"],
                    data={"quality": estimate.quality, "table_distance": estimate.distance, "standard_tables": estimate.standard_tables,
                          "luma_mean": estimate.luma_mean, "chroma_mean": estimate.chroma_mean, "sampling": jpeg.sampling,
                          "progressive": jpeg.progressive, "optimised_huffman": jpeg.optimised_huffman, "bits_per_pixel": bits_per_pixel,
                          "restart_interval": jpeg.restart_interval, "precision_bits": jpeg.precision, "components": jpeg.components},
                )  # fmt: skip

                if not estimate.standard_tables:
                    out.finding(
                        "notice",
                        "Compression tables are not a camera's",
                        "Cameras and most libraries scale the standard tables of the JPEG specification. These tables follow a different recipe, as "
                        "Photoshop, some web exporters and messaging apps use, so this copy was written by such software.",
                        tags=["jpeg", "software"],
                        data={"table_distance": estimate.distance, "luma_table": jpeg.quant[0].astype(int).tolist()},
                    )

            signs = []

            if jpeg.progressive:
                signs.append("progressive scan order (cameras write baseline)")

            if jpeg.optimised_huffman:
                signs.append("optimised Huffman tables (cameras write the standard tables)")

            if jpeg.sampling == "4:4:4" and (jpeg.components == 3):
                signs.append("no chroma subsampling (phones always subsample)")

            if jpeg.adobe is not None:
                signs.append("an APP14 'Adobe' marker")

            if jpeg.arithmetic:
                signs.append("arithmetic coding (very unusual)")

            if jpeg.exif_first is False and any("Exif" in a for a in jpeg.app_names):
                signs.append("a JFIF header placed before the Exif block (libjpeg-style re-save)")

            if signs:
                out.finding(
                    "notice",
                    "Encoder fingerprint: re-saved by software",
                    "The way this JPEG is written is not how a camera writes one: " + "; ".join(signs) + ". The picture passed through an editor, "
                    "converter, website or messaging app after capture. That alone does not mean the content changed.",
                    tags=["jpeg", "software", "resaved"],
                    data={"signs": signs, "app_segments": jpeg.app_names},
                )
            elif jpeg.exif_first and not jpeg.optimised_huffman and not jpeg.progressive:
                out.finding(
                    "info",
                    "Encoder fingerprint: camera-style JPEG",
                    "Exif block first, baseline scan, standard Huffman tables" + (f", {jpeg.sampling} subsampling" if jpeg.sampling != "?" else "") +
                    ": the way cameras and phones write a JPEG. Consistent with a file that has not been re-saved.",
                    tags=["jpeg", "camera"],
                    data={"app_segments": jpeg.app_names},
                )

            if jpeg.comments:
                out.finding(
                    "notice",
                    f"Comment inside the JPEG: “{jpeg.comments[0][:80]}”",
                    "A COM segment carries free text written by software or a person. Cameras never write one; libjpeg-based tools and some editors do.",
                    tags=["jpeg", "software", "text"],
                    data={"comments": jpeg.comments[:5]},
                )

        # ---- JPEG ghosts: earlier saves ---------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.3, "recompressing at every quality (JPEG ghosts)")
        ghost = await asyncio.to_thread(ghost_curve, image)
        curve = ghost["curve"]
        qualities = ghost["qualities"]
        current = published.get("quality")
        marks = {}

        if current:
            marks[f"this file ≈ q{current}"] = float(current)

        dips = ghost_minima(qualities, curve)
        earlier = [d for d in dips if current is None or abs(d["quality"] - current) >= 6]

        if earlier:
            marks[f"earlier save ≈ q{earlier[0]['quality']:.0f}"] = earlier[0]["quality"]

        out.artifact(
            "ghost", "series", "JPEG ghost curve: recompression error at each quality",
            data=downsample_series(qualities, {"mean squared error": curve}) | {"x_unit": "quality", "y_unit": "MSE", "marks": marks},
        )  # fmt: skip
        published["ghost_dips"] = dips

        if earlier and jpeg is not None:
            best = earlier[0]
            quality = int(best["quality"])
            maps = ghost["block_maps"].get(quality) or []
            lo = ghost["block_maps"].get(quality - 4) or ghost["block_maps"].get(quality - 2) or []
            hi = ghost["block_maps"].get(quality + 4) or ghost["block_maps"].get(quality + 2) or []
            region_words = ""

            if maps and lo and hi:
                # Where the dip is strongest: blocks that were once saved at that quality.
                strength = [np.clip(((a + b) / 2 - m) / ((a + b) / 2 + 1e-6), 0, 1) for m, a, b in zip(maps, lo, hi)]
                full = np.zeros((image.shape[0] // 16 + 1, image.shape[1] // 16 + 1), dtype=np.float32)
                size = ghost["size"]

                for (y, x), s in zip(ghost["corners"], strength):
                    full[y // 16 : y // 16 + s.shape[0], x // 16 : x // 16 + s.shape[1]] = np.maximum(full[y // 16 : y // 16 + s.shape[0], x // 16 : x // 16 + s.shape[1]], s)

                covered = full > 0
                heat = full / (np.percentile(full[covered], 99) + 1e-6) if covered.any() else full
                path = out.path("ghost_map.jpg")
                photo.save_bgr(path, photo.heat_overlay(photo.fit(image, 1600), cv2.resize(heat, (image.shape[1] // 4, image.shape[0] // 4)) if False else heat, cv2.COLORMAP_INFERNO, 0.7))
                out.artifact(
                    "ghost_map", "heatmap", f"JPEG ghost map at quality {quality}",
                    file=path, data={"caption": f"Bright: parts that recompress unusually well at quality {quality}, i.e. were saved at that quality before", "overlay": True},
                )  # fmt: skip
                fraction = float((full[covered] > 0.5 * full[covered].max()).mean()) if covered.any() else 0.0

                if 0.05 < fraction < 0.6 and covered.any():
                    ys, xs = np.where(full > 0.5 * full[covered].max())
                    box = photo.box_fraction(xs.min() * 16, ys.min() * 16, (xs.max() - xs.min() + 1) * 16, (ys.max() - ys.min() + 1) * 16, image.shape[1], image.shape[0])
                    region_words = f" The ghost is concentrated in one part of the picture (about {fraction * 100:.0f}% of the sampled area), which is how a region pasted in from a quality-{quality} JPEG looks."
                    published["ghost_region"] = box
                else:
                    box = None
            else:
                box = None

            out.finding(
                "warning" if best["depth"] >= 0.15 or box else "notice",
                f"Compressed twice: traces of an earlier save at quality ≈ {quality}",
                f"Recompressing the picture at every quality shows a dip of {best['depth'] * 100:.0f}% at quality {quality}, apart from the file's own quality"
                f"{f' ({current})' if current else ''}. A picture saved once has one dip; a second dip is the ghost of an earlier JPEG save.{region_words}",
                tags=["jpeg", "resaved", "double-compression"] + (["splice", "tamper"] if box else []),
                data={"earlier_quality": quality, "depth": best["depth"], "current_quality": current, "all_dips": dips, "box": box} if box else
                     {"earlier_quality": quality, "depth": best["depth"], "current_quality": current, "all_dips": dips},
            )  # fmt: skip
        elif jpeg is not None:
            out.finding(
                "info",
                "No ghost of an earlier JPEG save",
                "Recompressing at every quality shows a single dip at the file's own quality. Nothing points to a second JPEG generation"
                " (a re-save at a much higher quality than the first would hide one).",
                tags=["jpeg"],
                data={"dips": dips},
            )

        # ---- block grid -------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.7, "measuring the 8×8 block grid")
        col_profile, row_profile = await asyncio.to_thread(grid_profile, gray)
        phase_x, strength_x = grid_strength(col_profile)
        phase_y, strength_y = grid_strength(row_profile)
        strength = min(strength_x, strength_y)
        out.artifact(
            "grid_profile", "bars", "Edge energy by pixel position within the 8×8 grid",
            data={"labels": [f"col {k}" for k in range(8)] + [f"row {k}" for k in range(8)],
                  "values": np.round(np.concatenate([col_profile, row_profile]), 4).tolist()},
        )  # fmt: skip
        published["grid"] = {"phase": [phase_x, phase_y], "strength": strength}

        if jpeg is None and strength > 3.0 and phase_x == 0 and phase_y == 0:
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                f"This {info.format} was once a JPEG",
                f"An 8×8 block grid shows through the pixels ({strength:.1f} σ above the other positions). {info.format} is lossless and leaves no grid; "
                "the picture was a JPEG before it was converted. Screenshots of JPEGs and re-saved downloads look like this.",
                tags=["jpeg", "resaved", "converted"],
                data={"strength": strength, "col_profile": col_profile.tolist(), "row_profile": row_profile.tolist()},
            )
        elif jpeg is None and strength > 3.0:
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                f"JPEG grid offset by ({phase_x}, {phase_y}) pixels in this {info.format}",

                fraction_shifted = float(shifted.sum() / confident.sum())
                heat = np.where(shifted, np.clip(strengths / 8, 0, 1), 0).astype(np.float32)
                path = out.path("grid_map.jpg")
                photo.save_bgr(path, photo.heat_overlay(photo.fit(image, 1600), heat, cv2.COLORMAP_COOL, 0.7))

import importlib
from typing import Any

_VIDEO_MODULES = [
    ("earwitness.modules.provenance", "Provenance"),
    ("earwitness.modules.timeline", "Timeline"),
    ("earwitness.modules.spectrum", "Spectrum"),
    ("earwitness.modules.enf", "Enf"),
    ("earwitness.modules.light", "Light"),
    ("earwitness.modules.pulse", "Pulse"),
    ("earwitness.modules.tamper", "Tamper"),
    ("earwitness.modules.avsync", "AvSync"),
    ("earwitness.modules.ocr", "Ocr"),
    ("earwitness.modules.transcript", "Transcript"),
    ("earwitness.modules.sounds", "Sounds"),
    ("earwitness.modules.vision", "Vision"),
    ("earwitness.modules.geo", "Geo"),
    ("earwitness.modules.weather", "Weather"),
    ("earwitness.modules.brief", "Brief"),
]

# Still photographs: no clock, no sound, but every pixel and every byte of
# metadata at full resolution.
_IMAGE_MODULES = [
    ("earwitness.modules.photo_provenance", "PhotoProvenance"),
    ("earwitness.modules.compression", "Compression"),
    ("earwitness.modules.photo_pixels", "PhotoPixels"),
    ("earwitness.modules.hidden", "Hidden"),
    ("earwitness.modules.faces", "Faces"),
    ("earwitness.modules.synthetic", "Synthetic"),
    ("earwitness.modules.ocr", "Ocr"),
    ("earwitness.modules.vision", "Vision"),
    ("earwitness.modules.geo", "Geo"),
    ("earwitness.modules.weather", "Weather"),
    ("earwitness.modules.brief", "Brief"),
]

_BY_KIND = {"video": _VIDEO_MODULES, "image": _IMAGE_MODULES, "audio": _VIDEO_MODULES}


def all_modules(kind: str = "video") -> list[Any]:
    modules = []

    for path, cls in _BY_KIND.get(kind, _VIDEO_MODULES):
        try:
            module = importlib.import_module(path)
        except ModuleNotFoundError as error:
            if error.name == path:
                continue

            raise

        modules.append(getattr(module, cls)())

    return modules


def kinds() -> list[str]:
    return ["video", "image"]

def _image_proxy(case: Case, ctx: CaseContext) -> str | None:
    """A browser-viewable, upright JPEG of the photo (HEIC/TIFF/16-bit need one) plus a thumbnail."""
    from earwitness import photo

    image = ctx.image()

    if image is None:
        return None

    out = os.path.join(case.workdir, "proxy.jpg")
    photo.save_jpeg(out, photo.fit(image, 3000), 92)
    photo.save_jpeg(os.path.join(case.workdir, "thumb.jpg"), photo.thumbnail_of(image, 480), 85)

    return out

"""Run selected modules on one or more photos and print findings (no DB)."""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time

os.environ.setdefault("EARWITNESS_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)

from earwitness.server import jobs  # noqa: E402

async def _noop(case):
    return None

jobs._index = _noop


def run(path: str, modules: list[str] | None, keep: str | None = None) -> None:
    async def go():
        root = keep or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ew-")
        store = jobs.CaseStore(os.path.join(root, "cases"))
        case = store.create(path, {"original_name": os.path.basename(path)})
        shutil.copy(path, case.evidence_path)
        store.start(case, only=modules)
        await case.task
        return case

    t = time.time()
    case = asyncio.run(go())
    print(f"\n==== {os.path.basename(path)}  ({time.time() - t:.1f}s)  workdir={case.workdir}")
    for e in case.events:
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] in ("error", "skipped"):
            print(f"  [{e['status'].upper()} {e['module']}] {e.get('message')}")
            if e.get("trace"):
                print(e["trace"])
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] == "done":
            print(f"  [done {e['module']} {e.get('elapsed_s')}s]")
        if e["type"] == "finding":
            f = e["finding"]
            print(f"  {f['severity'][:4].upper():4} {f['module']:11} {f['title']}")
            if "-v" in sys.argv:
                print(f"       {f['detail']}")
                print(f"       {json.dumps(f['data'])[:300]}")
        if e["type"] == "artifact" and "-a" in sys.argv:
            a = e["artifact"]
            print(f"  art  {a['id']:28} {a['kind']:8} {a['title'][:70]} {a.get('url') or ''}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("-")]
    mods = None
    if args and args[0].startswith("mods="):
        mods = args[0][5:].split(",")
        args = args[1:]
    keep = os.environ.get("EW_KEEP")
    for p in args:
        run(p, mods, keep)

"""Run selected modules on one or more photos and print findings (no DB)."""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time

os.environ.setdefault("EARWITNESS_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)

from earwitness.server import jobs  # noqa: E402

async def _noop(case):
    return None

jobs._index = _noop


def run(path: str, modules: list[str] | None, keep: str | None = None) -> None:
    async def go():
        root = keep or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ew-")
        store = jobs.CaseStore(os.path.join(root, "cases"))
        case = store.create(path, {"original_name": os.path.basename(path)})
        shutil.copy(path, case.evidence_path)
        store.start(case, only=modules)
        await case.task
        return case

    t = time.time()
    case = asyncio.run(go())
    print(f"\n==== {os.path.basename(path)}  ({time.time() - t:.1f}s)  workdir={case.workdir}")
    for e in case.events:
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] in ("error", "skipped"):
            print(f"  [{e['status'].upper()} {e['module']}] {e.get('message')}")
            if e.get("trace"):
                print(e["trace"])
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] == "done":

        if e["type"] == "finding":
            f = e["finding"]
            print(f"  {f['severity'][:4].upper():4} {f['module']:11} {f['title']}")
            if "-v" in sys.argv:
                print(f"       {f['detail']}")
                print(f"       {json.dumps(f['data'])[:300]}")
        if e["type"] == "artifact" and "-a" in sys.argv:
            a = e["artifact"]
            print(f"  art  {a['id']:28} {a['kind']:8} {a['title'][:70]} {a.get('url') or ''}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("-")]
    mods = None
    if args and args[0].startswith("mods="):
        mods = args[0][5:].split(",")
        args = args[1:]

    for p in args:
        run(p, mods, keep)

"""Run selected modules on one or more photos and print findings (no DB)."""

import asyncio
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import time

os.environ.setdefault("EARWITNESS_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.pop("OPENAI_API_KEY", None)

from earwitness.server import jobs  # noqa: E402

async def _noop(case):
    return None

jobs._index = _noop


def run(path: str, modules: list[str] | None, keep: str | None = None) -> None:
    async def go():
        root = keep or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ew-")
        store = jobs.CaseStore(os.path.join(root, "cases"))
        case = store.create(path, {"original_name": os.path.basename(path)})
        shutil.copy(path, case.evidence_path)
        store.start(case, only=modules)
        await case.task
        return case

    t = time.time()
    case = asyncio.run(go())
    print(f"\n==== {os.path.basename(path)}  ({time.time() - t:.1f}s)  workdir={case.workdir}")
    for e in case.events:
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] in ("error", "skipped"):
            print(f"  [{e['status'].upper()} {e['module']}] {e.get('message')}")
            if e.get("trace"):
                print(e["trace"])
        if e["type"] == "module" and e["status"] == "done":
            print(f"  [done {e['module']} {e.get('elapsed_s')}s]")
        if e["type"] == "finding":
            f = e["finding"]
            print(f"  {f['severity'][:4].upper():4} {f['module']:11} {f['title']}")
            if "-v" in sys.argv:
                print(f"       {f['detail']}")
                print(f"       {json.dumps(f['data'])[:300]}")
        if e["type"] == "artifact" and "-a" in sys.argv:
            a = e["artifact"]
            print(f"  art  {a['id']:28} {a['kind']:8} {a['title'][:70]} {a.get('url') or ''}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("-")]
    mods = None
    if args and args[0].startswith("mods="):
        mods = args[0][5:].split(",")
        args = args[1:]
    keep = os.environ.get("EW_KEEP")
    for p in args:
        run(p, mods, keep)

    """(phase of the strongest boundary, how far it stands above the other phases, in sigmas).

    the opposite phase too; that is not a JPEG grid and scores zero.

    phase = int(np.argmax(profile))

"""Pixel forensics on a still photograph, at full resolution.

Video codecs reshape grain and recompress every frame, so on video these maps
are only for the eye. A photograph is one exposure saved once: here the same
analyses can be scored.

- Error level analysis at the file's own quality: a region pasted in from
  another JPEG recompresses differently from its surroundings.
- Noise residual consistency: one sensor leaves one grain; a patch with
  different grain was processed separately.
- Copy-move: SIFT self-matching (rotation and scale tolerant) finds a patch
  stamped elsewhere in the same picture.
- Resampling traces: resizing or rotating leaves periodic correlations between
  neighbouring pixels, visible as peaks in the spectrum of the prediction error.
- Histogram combing: contrast, levels and brightness adjustments leave gaps and
  spikes in the tone histogram.
- Luminance gradient, principal-component and amplified-noise views for a human
  examiner.
"""

import asyncio
from typing import Any

import cv2
import numpy as np

from earwitness import photo
from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext
from earwitness.modules.base import Reporter
from earwitness.modules.base import Skip
from earwitness.modules.tamper import _blocks
from earwitness.modules.tamper import _noise_map

_ANALYSIS_SIDE = 1600
_CLONE_SIDE = 2000
_BLOCK = 16


def _robust_z(values: np.ndarray, valid: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    sample = values[valid] if valid is not None and valid.any() else values
    median = np.median(sample)
    mad = np.median(np.abs(sample - median)) * 1.4826 + 1e-6

    return (values - median) / mad


def _ela(rgb: np.ndarray, quality: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(ELA map at pixel resolution, texture-normalised block z-scores)."""
    again = photo.decode_jpeg_bytes(photo.encode_jpeg_bytes(rgb, quality))

    if again is None or again.shape != rgb.shape:
        again = rgb

    diff = np.abs(rgb.astype(np.int16) - again.astype(np.int16)).max(axis=2).astype(np.float32)
    diff = cv2.blur(diff, (5, 5))
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(rgb, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
    energy = _blocks(diff, _BLOCK)
    brightness = _blocks(gray, _BLOCK)
    texture = _blocks(np.abs(cv2.Laplacian(cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (0, 0), 1.5), cv2.CV_32F)), _BLOCK)
    design = np.stack([np.ones_like(brightness), brightness / 255, (brightness / 255) ** 2, np.log1p(texture)], axis=-1)
    flat = design.reshape(-1, design.shape[-1])
    target = np.log1p(energy.reshape(-1))
    coefficients, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(flat, target, rcond=None)
    residual = (target - flat @ coefficients).reshape(energy.shape)
    valid = (brightness > 10) & (brightness < 245)
    z = np.where(valid, _robust_z(residual, valid), 0.0)

    return diff, z


def _regions(hot: np.ndarray, minimum_blocks: int, block: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    count, labels, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(hot.astype(np.uint8), connectivity=8)
    regions = []

    for s in stats[1:]:
        if s[4] >= minimum_blocks:
            regions.append({"x": int(s[0]) * block, "y": int(s[1]) * block, "w": int(s[2]) * block, "h": int(s[3]) * block, "blocks": int(s[4])})

    return sorted(regions, key=lambda r: -r["blocks"])


def _copy_move_sift(gray: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Self-matching SIFT keypoints that agree on one rigid motion."""
    sift = cv2.SIFT_create(nfeatures=8000, contrastThreshold=0.03)
    keypoints, descriptors = sift.detectAndCompute(gray, None)

    if descriptors is None or len(keypoints) < 60:
        return None

    matcher = cv2.BFMatcher(cv2.NORM_L2)
    knn = matcher.knnMatch(descriptors, descriptors, k=3)
    src, dst = [], []
    minimum_apart = 0.03 * max(gray.shape)

    for group in knn:
        if len(group) < 3:
            continue

        # group[0] is the point itself; the real nearest neighbour must beat the next one clearly.
        a, b = group[1], group[2]

        if a.distance > 0.6 * b.distance or a.distance > 220:
            continue

        p = np.array(keypoints[a.queryIdx].pt)
        q = np.array(keypoints[a.trainIdx].pt)

        if np.linalg.norm(p - q) >= minimum_apart:
            src.append(p)
            dst.append(q)

    if len(src) < 12:
        return None

    src_a, dst_a = np.float32(src), np.float32(dst)
    best: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    for _ in range(2):  # the first cluster, then (if any) a second distinct one
        if len(src_a) < 12:
            break

        transform, inliers = cv2.estimateAffinePartial2D(src_a, dst_a, method=cv2.RANSAC, ransacReprojThreshold=3.0, maxIters=4000, confidence=0.995)

        if transform is None or inliers is None:
            break

        mask = inliers.ravel().astype(bool)
        count = int(mask.sum())

        if count < 14:
            break

        a, b = transform[0, 0], transform[0, 1]
        scale = float(np.hypot(a, b))
        angle = float(np.degrees(np.arctan2(b, a)))
        shift = transform[:, 2]
        sources = src_a[mask]
        targets = dst_a[mask]
        spread = np.ptp(sources, axis=0)
        # Repeated real texture (windows, tiles, text) repeats everywhere; a clone is one compact patch.
        compact = spread.max() <= 0.5 * max(gray.shape)
        moved = np.linalg.norm(shift) > minimum_apart or abs(angle) > 3 or abs(scale - 1) > 0.05

        if compact and moved and count >= 0.35 * len(src_a):
            candidate = {
                "count": count,
                "total_pairs": int(len(src_a)),
                "scale": scale,
                "angle_deg": angle,
                "shift": [float(shift[0]), float(shift[1])],
                "source_box": [float(v) for v in (*sources.min(axis=0), *(sources.max(axis=0) - sources.min(axis=0)))],
                "target_box": [float(v) for v in (*targets.min(axis=0), *(targets.max(axis=0) - targets.min(axis=0)))],
                "pairs": [(tuple(map(int, s)), tuple(map(int, t))) for s, t in zip(sources, targets)],
            }

            if best is None or candidate["count"] > best["count"]:
                best = candidate

        src_a, dst_a = src_a[~mask], dst_a[~mask]

    return best


def _resampling(gray: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Popescu & Farid: periodic correlations from interpolation show as spectral peaks."""
    h, w = gray.shape
    side = min(1024, h, w)
    y0, x0 = (h - side) // 2, (w - side) // 2
    patch = gray[y0 : y0 + side, x0 : x0 + side].astype(np.float64)
    # 3x3 linear predictor fitted on the patch itself.
    pad = np.pad(patch, 1, mode="reflect")
    neighbours = [pad[1 + dy : 1 + dy + side, 1 + dx : 1 + dx + side].ravel() for dy in (-1, 0, 1) for dx in (-1, 0, 1) if (dy, dx) != (0, 0)]
    design = np.stack(neighbours, axis=1)
    target = patch.ravel()
    pick = np.random.default_rng(0).choice(len(target), size=min(len(target), 200_000), replace=False)
    coefficients, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(design[pick], target[pick], rcond=None)
    residual = (target - design @ coefficients).reshape(side, side)
    window = np.hanning(side)
    spectrum = np.abs(np.fft.fftshift(np.fft.fft2(residual * window[:, None] * window[None, :])))
    log = np.log1p(spectrum)
    background = cv2.medianBlur(log.astype(np.float32), 21)
    peaks = log - background
    centre = side // 2
    yy, xx = np.mgrid[:side, :side]
    fy, fx = (yy - centre) / side, (xx - centre) / side
    mask = np.ones_like(peaks, dtype=bool)
    mask &= np.hypot(fx, fy) > 0.03  # DC and very low frequencies
    # JPEG's 8x8 grid puts peaks at multiples of 1/8; ignore those (and their immediate surroundings).
    near_eighth = (np.abs((fx * 8) - np.round(fx * 8)) < 0.04) & (np.abs((fy * 8) - np.round(fy * 8)) < 0.04)
    mask &= ~near_eighth
    # Peaks on the axes or symmetric pairs are what interpolation produces.
    sigma = np.std(peaks[mask]) + 1e-9
    z = peaks / sigma
    z_masked = np.where(mask, z, 0)
    index = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(z_masked), z.shape)
    peak_z = float(z_masked[index])
    peak_f = (float(fx[index]), float(fy[index]))
    strong = int((z_masked > 6).sum())
    vis = np.clip((log - log.min()) / (np.ptp(log) + 1e-9) * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

    return {"peak_z": peak_z, "peak_frequency": peak_f, "strong_peaks": strong, "spectrum": vis, "coefficients": coefficients.tolist()}


def _histogram(gray: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    hist = np.bincount(gray.ravel(), minlength=256).astype(float)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(gray, 0.5), np.percentile(gray, 99.5)
    inner = np.arange(256)
    inside = (inner > lo + 2) & (inner < hi - 2)
    gaps = int(((hist == 0) & inside & (np.roll(hist, 1) > 0) & (np.roll(hist, -1) > 0)).sum())
    neighbours = (np.roll(hist, 1) + np.roll(hist, -1)) / 2 + 1
    spikes = int(((hist > 2.5 * neighbours) & inside & (hist > hist[inside].mean() * 0.2)).sum())
    used = int(((hist > 0) & inside).sum())
    total_inside = int(inside.sum())

    return {"hist": hist, "gaps": gaps, "spikes": spikes, "levels_used": used, "levels_inside": total_inside, "clipped_black": float(hist[:2].sum() / hist.sum()), "clipped_white": float(hist[254:].sum() / hist.sum())}


def _gradient_view(rgb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(rgb, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
    gx = cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0, ksize=3)
    gy = cv2.Sobel(gray, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1, ksize=3)
    magnitude = np.hypot(gx, gy)
    angle = (np.degrees(np.arctan2(gy, gx)) + 180) / 2  # 0..180 for OpenCV hue
    value = np.clip(magnitude / (np.percentile(magnitude, 99) + 1e-6) * 255, 0, 255)
    hsv = np.stack([angle.astype(np.uint8), np.full_like(angle, 255, dtype=np.uint8), value.astype(np.uint8)], axis=-1)

    return cv2.cvtColor(hsv, cv2.COLOR_HSV2BGR)


def _pca_views(rgb: np.ndarray) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    flat = rgb.reshape(-1, 3).astype(np.float32)
    mean = flat.mean(axis=0)
    centred = flat - mean
    sample = centred[np.random.default_rng(0).choice(len(centred), size=min(len(centred), 200_000), replace=False)]
    _, _, vt = np.linalg.svd(sample, full_matrices=False)
    views = []

    for component in vt:
        projected = centred @ component
        lo, hi = np.percentile(projected, 0.5), np.percentile(projected, 99.5)
        view = np.clip((projected - lo) / (hi - lo + 1e-6) * 255, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8).reshape(rgb.shape[:2])
        views.append(view)

    return views


def _noise_view(rgb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(rgb, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY).astype(np.float32)
    residual = gray - cv2.medianBlur(gray.astype(np.uint8), 3).astype(np.float32)

    return np.clip(residual * 10 + 128, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)


class PhotoPixels:
    name = "tamper"
    title = "PIXEL FORENSICS"
    description = "Error-level analysis at the file's own quality, grain consistency, SIFT copy-move, resampling traces, histogram combing, gradient/PCA/noise views."
    depends = ["jpeg"]

    async def run(self, ctx: CaseContext, out: Reporter) -> None:
        image = ctx.image()
        info = ctx.image_info()

        if image is None or info is None:
            raise Skip("not a decodable image")

        compression = await ctx.wait_for("jpeg") or {}
        is_jpeg = bool(compression.get("is_jpeg"))
        quality = int(compression.get("quality") or 90)
        full_w, full_h = image.shape[1], image.shape[0]
        analysis = photo.fit(image, _ANALYSIS_SIDE)
        scale = analysis.shape[1] / full_w
        published: dict[str, Any] = {"regions": [], "boxes": []}
        flagged = 0

        def frac(region: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
            return photo.box_fraction(region["x"] / scale, region["y"] / scale, region["w"] / scale, region["h"] / scale, full_w, full_h)

        # ---- ELA -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.05, "error level analysis")
        ela_quality = min(max(quality, 50), 95) if is_jpeg else 90
        ela, ela_z = await asyncio.to_thread(_ela, analysis, ela_quality)
        ela_heat = np.clip(ela / (np.percentile(ela, 99.5) + 1e-6), 0, 1).astype(np.float32)
        ela_path = out.path("ela.jpg")
        photo.save_bgr(ela_path, photo.heat_overlay(analysis, ela_heat))
        out.artifact("ela", "heatmap", f"Error-level analysis (re-saved at quality {ela_quality})", file=ela_path,
                     data={"caption": "bright = recompresses differently from its surroundings", "overlay": True})  # fmt: skip
        raw_ela_path = out.path("ela_raw.png")
        cv2.imwrite(raw_ela_path, np.clip(ela * (255 / (np.percentile(ela, 99.5) + 1e-6)), 0, 255).astype(np.uint8))
        out.artifact("ela_raw", "image", "Error levels alone (no photo underneath)", file=raw_ela_path,
                     data={"caption": "Equal grey everywhere means one JPEG generation; a region that glows or goes dark was saved separately"})  # fmt: skip
        ela_regions = _regions(ela_z > 4.0, 10, _BLOCK)
        texture_ok = [r for r in ela_regions if r["w"] * r["h"] < 0.35 * analysis.shape[0] * analysis.shape[1]]

        if texture_ok and is_jpeg:
            region = texture_ok[0]
            flagged += 1
            box = frac(region)
            published["boxes"].append(box)
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                "Region recompresses differently from the rest",
                f"After allowing for brightness and texture, a {region['w'] / scale:.0f}×{region['h'] / scale:.0f} px area ({region['blocks']} blocks) has error levels far above the picture's norm. "
                "Everything saved in one JPEG generation ages the same way; a patch that behaves differently was pasted in or edited and saved again."
                + (f" {len(texture_ok) - 1} smaller such area{'s' if len(texture_ok) > 2 else ''} too." if len(texture_ok) > 1 else ""),
                tags=["tamper", "ela", "splice"],
                data={"box": box, "blocks": region["blocks"], "regions": [frac(r) for r in texture_ok[:5]], "quality": ela_quality},
            )

        # ---- grain consistency -----------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.25, "grain consistency")
        noise_z = await asyncio.to_thread(_noise_map, analysis)
        noise_heat = np.clip(np.abs(noise_z) / 8, 0, 1).astype(np.float32)
        noise_path = out.path("noise.jpg")
        photo.save_bgr(noise_path, photo.heat_overlay(analysis, noise_heat))
        out.artifact("noise", "heatmap", "Noise-residual map", file=noise_path,
                     data={"caption": "bright = grain unlike the rest of the picture (after allowing for brightness and texture)", "overlay": True})  # fmt: skip
        hot = np.abs(noise_z) > 5.0
        noise_regions = [r for r in _regions(hot, 12, 24) if r["w"] * r["h"] < 0.3 * analysis.shape[0] * analysis.shape[1]]

        if noise_regions:
            region = noise_regions[0]
            direction = "less" if np.median(noise_z[region["y"] // 24 : (region["y"] + region["h"]) // 24, region["x"] // 24 : (region["x"] + region["w"]) // 24]) < 0 else "more"
            box = frac(region)
            published["boxes"].append(box)
            flagged += 1
            out.finding(
                "warning",
                f"Grain differs in one region ({direction} noise than the rest)",
                f"A {region['w'] / scale:.0f}×{region['h'] / scale:.0f} px area carries {direction} sensor grain than the model of this picture predicts for its brightness and texture. "
                "One sensor, one exposure, one grain: a patch that differs was smoothed, pasted from another photo, or generated. Heavy bokeh and smooth skies can also do this; check the map.",
                tags=["tamper", "noise"],
                data={"box": box, "blocks": region["blocks"], "regions": [frac(r) for r in noise_regions[:5]]},
            )

        # ---- copy-move ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.4, "searching for cloned patches")
        clone_image = photo.fit(image, _CLONE_SIDE)
        clone_scale = clone_image.shape[1] / full_w
        clone = await asyncio.to_thread(_copy_move_sift, cv2.cvtColor(clone_image, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY))

        if clone:
            flagged += 1
            canvas = cv2.cvtColor(clone_image, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR).copy()

            for a, b in clone["pairs"][:200]:
                cv2.line(canvas, a, b, (80, 220, 255), 1, cv2.LINE_AA)
                cv2.circle(canvas, a, 3, (60, 60, 255), -1)
                cv2.circle(canvas, b, 3, (60, 255, 120), -1)

            for key, colour in (("source_box", (60, 60, 255)), ("target_box", (60, 255, 120))):
                x, y, w, h = (int(v) for v in clone[key])
                cv2.rectangle(canvas, (x, y), (x + w, y + h), colour, 2)

            path = out.path("clone.jpg")
            photo.save_bgr(path, canvas)
            out.artifact("clone", "image", "Copy-move matches (red: source, green: copy)", file=path)
            sx, sy, sw, sh = clone["source_box"]
            tx, ty, tw, th = clone["target_box"]
            src_box = photo.box_fraction(sx / clone_scale, sy / clone_scale, sw / clone_scale, sh / clone_scale, full_w, full_h)
            dst_box = photo.box_fraction(tx / clone_scale, ty / clone_scale, tw / clone_scale, th / clone_scale, full_w, full_h)
            published["boxes"] += [src_box, dst_box]
            motion = []

            if np.hypot(*clone["shift"]) > 5:
                motion.append(f"moved ({clone['shift'][0] / clone_scale:+.0f}, {clone['shift'][1] / clone_scale:+.0f}) px")

            if abs(clone["angle_deg"]) > 1:
                motion.append(f"rotated {clone['angle_deg']:+.1f}°")

            if abs(clone["scale"] - 1) > 0.02:
                motion.append(f"scaled ×{clone['scale']:.2f}")

            out.finding(
                "critical" if clone["count"] >= 40 else "warning",
                "Cloned region: one patch appears twice",
                f"{clone['count']} distinctive feature points in one area reappear elsewhere in the same picture under a single rigid motion ({', '.join(motion) or 'in place'}). "
                "Cloning stamps one area over another to hide or duplicate something. Genuinely repeated objects (tiles, windows, text) can match too; check the two boxes.",
                tags=["tamper", "clone", "splice"],
                data={"box": dst_box, "source_box": src_box, "matches": clone["count"], "of_pairs": clone["total_pairs"],
                      "shift_px": [clone["shift"][0] / clone_scale, clone["shift"][1] / clone_scale], "angle_deg": clone["angle_deg"], "scale": clone["scale"]},
            )  # fmt: skip

        # ---- resampling ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.6, "resampling traces")
        gray_full = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
        resampling = await asyncio.to_thread(_resampling, gray_full)
        spectrum_path = out.path("resampling_spectrum.png")
        cv2.imwrite(spectrum_path, cv2.resize(resampling["spectrum"], (512, 512), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA))
        out.artifact("resampling", "image", "Spectrum of the pixel-prediction error", file=spectrum_path,
                     data={"caption": "A camera-original photo is a smooth cloud. Bright isolated dots are periodic correlations left by resizing, rotating or upscaling."})  # fmt: skip
        published["resampling_peak_z"] = resampling["peak_z"]

        if resampling["peak_z"] >= 9.0 and resampling["strong_peaks"] <= 60:
            fx, fy = resampling["peak_frequency"]
            period = 1 / max(1e-6, np.hypot(fx, fy))
            out.finding(
                "notice",
                "Resampled after capture (resized, rotated or upscaled)",
                f"The error of predicting each pixel from its neighbours repeats every {period:.1f} px (peak {resampling['peak_z']:.0f} σ above the spectral background). "
                "Interpolation leaves exactly this rhythm; camera sensors do not. Digital zoom, resizing for the web, rotation and AI upscaling all count.",
                tags=["resampled", "software"],
                data={"peak_z": resampling["peak_z"], "period_px": period, "frequency": [fx, fy], "strong_peaks": resampling["strong_peaks"]},
            )

        # ---- histogram -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.75, "tone histogram")
        hist = await asyncio.to_thread(_histogram, gray_full)
        out.artifact("histogram", "series", "Brightness histogram",
                     data={"x": list(range(256)), "series": [{"name": "pixels", "y": hist["hist"].tolist()}], "x_unit": "level", "y_unit": "pixels"})  # fmt: skip
        published["histogram"] = {k: v for k, v in hist.items() if k != "hist"}

        if hist["gaps"] + hist["spikes"] >= 12:
            out.finding(
                "notice",
                f"Tone curve applied: {hist['gaps']} gaps and {hist['spikes']} spikes in the histogram",
                "Stretching contrast, lifting shadows or changing brightness in 8-bit software leaves a comb of empty and over-full levels. A camera writes a smooth histogram. "
                "This is an adjustment, not necessarily a deception.",
                tags=["software", "adjusted"],
                data={k: v for k, v in hist.items() if k != "hist"},
            )

        if hist["clipped_white"] > 0.08 or hist["clipped_black"] > 0.12:
            out.finding(
                "info",
                f"{max(hist['clipped_white'], hist['clipped_black']) * 100:.0f}% of pixels clipped to pure {'white' if hist['clipped_white'] > hist['clipped_black'] else 'black'}",
                "Large flat areas of pure white or black hold no detail at all: nothing can be recovered there by enhancement.",
                tags=["exposure"],
                data={"clipped_white": hist["clipped_white"], "clipped_black": hist["clipped_black"]},
            )

        # ---- examiner's views ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        out.progress(0.85, "examiner's views")
        gradient = await asyncio.to_thread(_gradient_view, analysis)
        gradient_path = out.path("gradient.jpg")
        photo.save_bgr(gradient_path, gradient)
        out.artifact("gradient", "heatmap", "Luminance gradient (colour = direction light falls)", file=gradient_path,
                     data={"caption": "Hue shows the direction of brightness change at each edge. Lit the same way, all objects share the same hue pattern; a pasted object lit differently stands out.", "overlay": True})  # fmt: skip
        pcas = await asyncio.to_thread(_pca_views, analysis)

        for index, view in enumerate(pcas[1:], start=2):
            pca_path = out.path(f"pca{index}.jpg")
            cv2.imwrite(pca_path, view, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 88])
            out.artifact(f"pca{index}", "heatmap", f"Principal component {index} of the colours", file=pca_path,
                         data={"caption": "Colour variation the eye hardly sees. Edits made in a different colour space, and halos around pasted objects, show up here.", "overlay": True})  # fmt: skip

        noise_view = await asyncio.to_thread(_noise_view, analysis)
        noise_view_path = out.path("noise_view.png")
        cv2.imwrite(noise_view_path, noise_view)
        out.artifact("noise_view", "heatmap", "Sensor grain, amplified 10×", file=noise_view_path,
                     data={"caption": "The grain itself. It should look like fine, even sand everywhere; a region that is smooth, blotchy or differently textured was processed separately.", "overlay": True})  # fmt: skip

        if not flagged:
            out.finding(
                "info",
                "No pasted or cloned regions found",
                "Error levels, grain and feature matching are consistent across the picture: nothing a copy-paste or clone stamp usually leaves. "
                "A skilled edit saved at high quality can pass these tests; the maps are attached for a human eye.",
                tags=["tamper"],
            )

        published["flagged"] = flagged
        ctx.publish(self.name, published)
        out.progress(1.0)
